definition_zh: 季节性；随季节波动的性质与幅度
definition_en: the quality or degree to which something varies with the seasons
core_image: 一条折线在十二个月里起落，最高点每年挤在同几个月，像被季节牵着走
scene: 岛上旅馆冬天大多空着，夏天要提前几个月才订得到房。 Tourism on the island shows strong seasonality, with empty hotels every winter.
sceneCN: 这里 seasonality 指「随季节起伏的性质与幅度」（第 1 个义项：季节性）；句意为岛上旅游业季节性很强，每到冬天旅馆空空。图中可辨识物件：空荡的泳池、落下的遮阳伞、旅馆前台、结霜的窗。

pos.zh: 季节性；随季节波动的性质与幅度（不可数；指具体季节型态时可数，复数 seasonalities）

forms.label: 复数（指不同的季节型态）

derivatives.zh: seasonal（基础形容词；seasonality 由 seasonal + -ity 状态名词后缀构成）→ 随季节变化的
seasonal + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以随季节的方式
satio（拉丁「播种」）经古法语 seson → 季节；另有一条「调味」义线

senses.title: The property of varying with the seasons
senses.definition: the tendency of a quantity or activity to rise and fall with the time of year
senses.definitionCN: 某一数量或活动随一年中的时节起落的倾向
senses.example: Tourism on the island shows strong seasonality, with empty hotels every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上旅游业季节性很强，每到冬天旅馆空空。
senses.why: The suffix -ity turns the adjective seasonal into a named property, just as national becomes nationality.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ity 把形容词 seasonal 变成一种被命名的性质，正如 national 变成 nationality。

senses.title: The size of the seasonal swing
senses.definition: the measured difference between the busy peak and the quiet trough of the year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中繁忙高峰与冷清低谷之间测得的差值
senses.example: Seasonality of ten to one makes staffing almost impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 十比一的季节落差让排班几乎无法安排。
senses.why: Once the property is measured, it becomes a number, and the noun names that number's size.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种性质被测量，它就变成一个数，而这个名词指这个数的大小。

senses.title: The tourist high and low season
senses.titleCN: 旅游业的旺季与淡季规律
senses.definition: the pattern in which visitors arrive in a few months and almost vanish in others
senses.definitionCN: 游客在少数几个月涌入、其余月份几乎消失的模式
senses.example: A second festival was invented to break the seasonality of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 为了打断海岸的季节性，人们又造了一个节庆。
senses.why: Holidays follow school terms and weather, so the trade inherits a sharp calendar from its customers.
senses.whyCN: 假期跟随学期与天气，因此这个行业从顾客那里继承了一张陡峭的日历。

senses.title: Seasonal distribution of a disease
senses.titleCN: 疾病在一年中的季节分布
senses.definition: the tendency of an infection to peak at a particular time of year
senses.definitionCN: 某种感染在一年中特定时段达到高峰的倾向
senses.example: The seasonality of influenza peaks in cold, dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 流感的季节性在寒冷干燥的月份达到高峰。
senses.why: Epidemiologists use the word for any repeated calendar pattern in case numbers, whether the cause is climate or behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学家用这个词指病例数中任何重复的日历模式，无论起因是气候还是行为。

senses.title: The seasonal rhythm of an ecosystem
senses.definition: the regular yearly cycle of leafing, flowering, breeding and decay in a community of organisms
senses.definitionCN: 生物群落中长叶、开花、繁殖与分解的年度规律循环
senses.example: Satellite images reveal the seasonality of green cover across the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像显示出三角洲绿色覆盖的季节性。
senses.why: Ecology measures the pattern as a whole, so the noun suits a community better than a single organism's response.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这一模式作为整体来测量，因此这个名词更适合群落，而非单个生物的反应。

senses.title: A component in time-series statistics
senses.titleCN: 时间序列统计中的季节成分
senses.definition: the part of a data series that repeats every year and can be estimated and removed
senses.definitionCN: 数据序列中每年重复、可被估计并剔除的部分
senses.example: The model separates seasonality from the underlying trend.
senses.exampleCN: 模型把季节性从底层趋势中分离出来。
senses.why: Statistics treats the calendar swing as one additive or multiplicative component, hence a countable technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把日历摆动当作一个可加或可乘的成分，因此产生可数的技术义。

senses.title: The harvest calendar of farming
senses.definition: the concentration of sowing, labour and income into a few weeks of the agricultural year
senses.definitionCN: 把播种、劳力与收入集中在农事年少数几周的情况
senses.example: Grain seasonality decides the price of farm labour each August.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物的季节性决定每年八月农工的价格。
senses.why: Farming is the original source of the word, so its calendar is the clearest case of the property.
senses.whyCN: 农业是这个词最古老的来源，因此它的日历是这种性质最清楚的例子。

senses.title: Seasonal demand for energy
senses.definition: the yearly pattern in which heating or cooling loads rise and fall with temperature
senses.definitionCN: 取暖或制冷负荷随温度起落的年度模式
senses.example: Gas seasonality forces utilities to buy storage capacity in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 天然气的季节性迫使公用事业在夏季购买储气能力。
senses.why: Energy demand is driven by the same weather calendar, so the property appears wherever a load is plotted against months.
senses.whyCN: 能源需求受同一张天气日历驱动，因此只要把负荷按月作图，这种性质就会出现。

intro.en: Seasonality is seasonal plus -ity, a Latin state-noun suffix. The base season comes from Latin satio 'a sowing'; the abstract noun itself is a modern formation whose exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: seasonality 是 seasonal 加 -ity（拉丁状态名词后缀）。基础词 season 来自拉丁 satio「播种」；这个抽象名词本身是近代构词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Serere 'to sow' gave satio 'a sowing', which passed through Old French as seson and became English season.
items.cn: serere「播种」生出 satio「播种」，经古法语 seson 成为英语 season。

items.en: The noun extended from sowing time to the four divisions of the year, and then to any marked period such as a football season.
items.cn: 这个名词从播种时节扩展到一年四季，再扩展到任何被标记的时期，如足球赛季。

items.en: The adjective seasonal is recorded in the nineteenth century, formed with the Latin suffix -alis. Its exact first year varies between sources.
items.cn: 形容词 seasonal 的书证见于十九世纪，由拉丁后缀 -alis 构成。各家记载的确切年份有出入。

items.en: The suffix -ity descends from Latin -itas, which turns an adjective into a name for a quality, as in nationality or porosity.
items.cn: 后缀 -ity 来自拉丁 -itas，把形容词变成性质名称，如 nationality、porosity。

items.en: Seasonality became common in economics, tourism and epidemiology in the twentieth century; the first written use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: seasonality 在二十世纪的经济学、旅游学与流行病学中变得常用；最早书面用例没有确切年代。

items.en: Time-series statistics later defined seasonality as an estimable component, giving the word a quantitative edge.
items.cn: 时间序列统计学后来把季节性定义为一个可估计的成分，使这个词带上量化色彩。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same season family that differ by suffix; group two holds nouns for regular variation in time.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 season 词族、仅后缀不同的形式；第二组是表示时间上有规律变化的名称。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a thing that varies by season; seasonality is the abstract property, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 描述随季节变化之物的形容词；seasonality 是抽象性质，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: From season plus -able: 'fitting the season', as seasonable weather; it judges suitability, not periodicity.
entries.definitionCN: season 加 -able，意为「合于时令的」，如合时的天气；评判合宜性，而非周期性。

entries.definition: The participle of the culinary or experiential verb season; nothing to do with yearly cycles.
entries.definitionCN: 烹饪或经验动词 season 的分词；与年度周期无关。

entries.definition: The noun for salt, herbs and spices, from the separate 'to flavour' line of season.
entries.definitionCN: 指盐、香草与香料的名词，来自 season 另一条「调味」义线。

entries.definition: The property of repeating at fixed intervals of any length; seasonality is the yearly special case.
entries.definitionCN: 以任意固定间隔重复的性质；seasonality 是其中以年为单位的特例。

entries.definition: The tendency to move in cycles, often economic; the cycle may be longer or shorter than a year.
entries.definitionCN: 沿周期运动的倾向，常用于经济；周期可长于或短于一年。

entries.definition: The general fact of changing, with no calendar attached; seasonality specifies a yearly pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 变化的一般事实，不附带日历；seasonality 特指年度模式。

entries.definition: An irregular up-and-down movement, often short-term; seasonality is regular and calendar-bound.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则的上下波动，常为短期；seasonality 是规律且绑定日历的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Seasonal plus -ity equals the name of the property, as national plus -ity gives nationality.
normal.cn: seasonal 加 -ity 得到性质名称，正如 national 加 -ity 得到 nationality。

normal.en: The family runs season, seasonal, seasonally, seasonality, seasonable, off-season.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 season、seasonal、seasonally、seasonality、seasonable、off-season。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: strong seasonality, seasonality of tourism, seasonality in demand.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：强烈的季节性、旅游业的季节性、需求的季节性。

normal.en: Seasonality is what a time-series analyst removes to see the true trend.
normal.cn: seasonality 正是时间序列分析者要减掉、以便看清真实趋势的东西。

normal.en: The stress falls late: sea-son-AL-i-ty, not SEASON-ality.
normal.cn: 重音靠后：sea-son-AL-i-ty，而非把重音放在 season 上。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that repeats its shape every twelve months.
abstract.cn: 想象一道每十二个月重复同一形状的波。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with two doors, one open in summer and one in winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一家有两扇门的店，夏天开一扇，冬天开另一扇。

abstract.en: Picture a graph stripped of its hills to show the slow climb beneath.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被削去山丘的图，露出底下缓慢的爬升。

examples.en: Tourism on the island shows strong seasonality, with empty hotels every winter.
examples.cn: 岛上旅游业季节性很强，每到冬天旅馆空空。

examples.en: The model separates seasonality from the underlying trend.
examples.cn: 模型把季节性从底层趋势中分离出来。

examples.en: Gas seasonality forces utilities to buy storage capacity in summer.
examples.cn: 天然气的季节性迫使公用事业在夏季购买储气能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四季呢，累题」——四季轮着来，题目年年重复 → 季节性

root: season 经古法语 seson 来自拉丁 satio「播种」，由 serere「播种」构成；-al 为形容词后缀，-ity 来自拉丁 -itas 性质名词后缀。英语 seasonality。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a line that rises and falls on a yearly clock. The shape is named as a property, then measured, then found in tourism, disease, ecology, statistics, farming and energy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：一条随年度时钟起落的线。这个形状先被命名为性质，再被测量，然后在旅游、疾病、生态、统计、农业与能源中出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a graph whose hill sits in the same months every year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张每年山丘都落在同样几个月的图。

branches.en: NAMED AND MEASURED: the property is first a quality, then a size on a scale.
branches.cn: 命名与测量：这种性质先是一种品质，再成为刻度上的大小。

branches.en: DEMAND CALENDAR: tourists and power loads both follow the same yearly hill.
branches.cn: 需求日历：游客与电力负荷都追随同一座年度山丘。

branches.en: DISEASE CALENDAR: infections also peak on a yearly schedule.
branches.cn: 疾病日历：感染也按年度时间表达到高峰。

branches.en: ECOSYSTEM RHYTHM: green cover and breeding repeat as a whole-community pattern.
branches.cn: 生态节律：绿色覆盖与繁殖作为群落整体模式重复。

branches.en: COMPONENT AND HARVEST: statistics isolates it, farming lives by it.
branches.cn: 成分与收获：统计学把它分离出来，农业则靠它生活。

intro.en: Seasonality stacks two Latin suffixes on a French-shaped English noun, so each layer can be peeled off and named.
intro.cn: seasonality 在一个法语外形的英语名词上叠了两层拉丁后缀，因此每一层都能剥开命名。

latinIntro.en: Satio 'a sowing' becomes English season; -alis makes seasonal; -itas makes the abstract noun. No Latin word seasonality itself existed.
latinIntro.cn: satio「播种」成为英语 season；-alis 构成 seasonal；-itas 构成抽象名词。拉丁语中并无 seasonality 这个词本身。

items.structure: Old French seson, from Latin satio
items.example: The dry season lasts four months.
The resort closes in the off-season.
Nationality and porosity follow the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: nationality 与 porosity 遵循同一模式。

definition_zh: 包含的；包括在内的；包容的（不排斥任何群体）；（范围）含端点的
definition_en: including a particular person, group or limit rather than leaving it out
core_image: 一圈人围坐，桌子原本留着一个缺口，后来缺口处也摆上一把椅子，圈就此闭合
scene: 礼堂的座位原本只排到侧门，工作人员又搬来几把椅子，把最后一排补满。 An inclusive admissions policy welcomes applicants from every region and every income level.
sceneCN: 这里指「不排斥任何群体、把所有人都纳入」（第 1 个义项：范围上包含所有人）；句意为不排斥的招生政策欢迎来自每个地区和每个收入水平的申请者。可辨识物件：礼堂座椅、侧门、登记桌、名单、台阶。

pos.zh: 包容的；不排斥任何群体的
包括在内的；含（某物）的
（范围）含端点的；全部费用在内的

senses.title: Leaving no group out
senses.definition: including everyone in a group, service or institution, especially people who are often excluded
senses.definitionCN: 把一个群体、服务或机构向所有人开放，尤其是常被排除在外的人
senses.example: An inclusive admissions policy welcomes applicants from every region and every income level.
senses.exampleCN: 不排斥的招生政策欢迎来自每个地区和每个收入水平的申请者。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in'; an inclusive rule shuts the gate only after everyone has been brought inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「关在里面」；一条包容的规则是在所有人都被带进来之后才关门。

senses.title: Including the stated item
senses.titleCN: 把所提到的事物包括在内
senses.definition: covering a named item as part of a total, often in the phrase inclusive of
senses.definitionCN: 把提到的事物计入总数，常用于「包括……在内」这一说法
senses.example: The quoted price is inclusive of delivery and insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 所报价格包含运费与保险。
senses.why: The word marks the boundary of a total: what lies inside the line is counted, what lies outside is not.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出总数的边界：线内之物计入，线外之物不计。

senses.title: One price covering everything
senses.titleCN: 一价全包、费用全部计入
senses.definition: describing a price or package that covers all costs, so no extra charge follows
senses.definitionCN: 描述涵盖全部费用的价格或套餐，事后不再另收费
senses.example: They booked an all-inclusive stay where meals and transfers were covered.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了一次一价全包的行程，餐食与接送都包含在内。
senses.why: The boundary sense turned commercial: the total is closed, and nothing is left outside it to be billed later.
senses.whyCN: 边界义进入商业语境：总数被封闭起来，外面不再留下任何可另行收费的项目。

senses.title: Counting both endpoints
senses.definition: counting the first and last values as part of a stated range
senses.definitionCN: 把所给范围的首尾数值都计入其中
senses.example: Read pages ten to twenty inclusive before the seminar.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课之前读完第十页到第二十页，含首尾两页。
senses.why: A closed interval is drawn with solid ends; the word says the ends are inside the line, not outside it.
senses.whyCN: 闭区间用实心端点画出；这个词表示端点在线内，而不在线外。

senses.title: Language that names everyone
senses.titleCN: 照顾到所有人的语言表达
senses.definition: using words that do not assume one gender, culture or group and leave others invisible
senses.definitionCN: 使用不预设某一种性别、文化或群体、也不让其他人隐形的措辞
senses.example: The style guide recommends inclusive language that names both parents.
senses.exampleCN: 体例指南建议使用同时提到双亲的包容性措辞。
senses.why: A phrase can have a margin too: whichever group is not named is left outside the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞也有边缘：没有被提到的那群人就留在句子之外。

senses.title: Classrooms built for all pupils
senses.titleCN: 让所有学生都能参与的课堂
senses.definition: describing schooling in which pupils with different needs learn together with shared support
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同需求的学生在共同支持下一起学习的教育安排
senses.example: The district moved toward inclusive classrooms with shared support staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区转向融合课堂，并配备共享的支持人员。
senses.why: The social sense settled into education, where the test of inclusion is whether a pupil sits inside the ordinary room.
senses.whyCN: 社会义进入教育领域，衡量的标准就是学生是否被安置在普通教室里。

senses.title: Growth that reaches the edge
senses.definition: describing economic growth that raises incomes and opportunities for low-income groups as well as the average
senses.definitionCN: 描述不仅提高平均值、也提高低收入群体收入与机会的经济增长
senses.example: Economists now ask whether growth is inclusive, not merely fast.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家现在追问增长是否包容，而不只看它是否快速。
senses.why: If growth stays in the centre, the margin receives nothing; an inclusive economy carries the gain to the edge.
senses.whyCN: 增长若只留在中心，边缘什么也得不到；包容的经济把收益带到边缘。

senses.title: A pronoun that includes the listener
senses.titleCN: 语言学中把听者包括在内的代词
senses.definition: describing a first person plural form that includes the person addressed as well as the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 描述既包括说话者、也包括受话者的第一人称复数形式
senses.example: In some languages an inclusive first person plural includes the listener.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言的第一人称复数包含式把听者也包括在内。
senses.why: Grammar drew the same line: an inclusive form keeps the listener inside the circle, an exclusive form leaves the listener outside.
senses.whyCN: 语法沿用了同一条界线：包含式把听者留在圈内，排除式把听者留在圈外。

intro.en: Inclusive comes from Medieval Latin inclusivus, from Latin includere 'to shut in', built on in- 'in' and claudere 'to shut, close'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inclusive 来自中世纪拉丁 inclusivus，再往上出自拉丁 includere「关在里面」，由 in-「在内」与 claudere「关闭」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Claudere meant 'to shut, close, enclose'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes suggested to clavis 'key' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: claudere 意为「关闭、围住」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与 clavis「钥匙」联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: In- 'in' plus claudere produced includere 'to shut in, enclose, include'.
items.cn: in-「在内」加 claudere 构成 includere「关在里面、围住、包括」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed inclusivus to describe something that encloses or counts another item within it.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构成 inclusivus，用来描述把另一项围在或计入自身之内的事物。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of enclosing or comprising.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个形容词，最初表示「围住」或「包含」。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was applied to schools, workplaces and growth, where the question is who is left outside the gate.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词被用于学校、职场与经济增长，问题变成谁被留在门之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of claudere is unsettled, and no exact first citation is recorded for the social sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：claudere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，社会义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same shutting-in root in other parts of speech; group two holds adjectives of wide or welcoming scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「关在里面」词根、词性不同的词；第二组是表示范围宽广或态度欢迎的形容词。

entries.definition: To bring something inside a group or total; inclusive is the adjective describing such a total.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带入一个群体或总数；inclusive 是描述这种总数的形容词。

entries.definition: Means 'having been counted in'; it marks an item already inside, while inclusive marks the boundary that lets it in.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「已被计入的」；它标记已在内部的项目，而 inclusive 标记放它进来的那条边界。

entries.definition: The act or state of being brought inside; the adjective describes the quality, the noun names the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 被带入内部的动作或状态；形容词描述性质，名词指事物本身。

entries.definition: Means in a way that leaves nothing out; it modifies how a list or rule is applied.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以不遗漏任何一项的方式」；修饰清单或规则被适用的方式。

entries.definition: Covering all or nearly all parts of a subject; it stresses completeness of content, not openness to people.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖一个主题的全部或几乎全部；强调内容的完整，而非对人的开放。

entries.definition: Describing a place or person that makes outsiders feel wanted; it names the emotional effect of inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 描述让外来者感到被接纳的场所或人；它指包容带来的情感效果。

entries.definition: Covering a wide range; it can describe a category without saying who is treated fairly inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖范围广；可描述一个类别，却不说明其中谁被公平对待。

entries.definition: Applying to every member without exception; stronger than inclusive because it allows no local variation.
entries.definitionCN: 无例外地适用于每一成员；比 inclusive 更强，因为它不留地方性差异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real shutting-in root, the real derivatives and the real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「关在里面」词根、真实的派生词与真实的政策搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in', so an inclusive rule closes the door only after everyone is inside.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「关在里面」，因此包容的规则是在所有人都进来之后才关门。

normal.en: The family runs include, included, inclusion, inclusive, inclusively, inclusiveness and inclusivity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 include、included、inclusion、inclusive、inclusively、inclusiveness 与 inclusivity。

normal.en: Policy phrases mark the modern sense: inclusive education, inclusive growth, inclusive language, all-inclusive.
normal.cn: 政策搭配标出现代义：融合教育、包容性增长、包容性语言、一价全包。

normal.en: The boundary sense survives in the arithmetic phrase 'ten to twenty inclusive'.
normal.cn: 边界义保留在算术说法「第十到第二十，含首尾」中。

normal.en: The prefix in- also appears in include and inclusion, all from the same Latin verb.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 同样出现在 include 与 inclusion 中，都出自同一个拉丁动词。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs with one gap, and a late guest filling that gap so the circle closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子留着一个缺口，一位迟到的客人坐进缺口，圆圈就此闭合。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that stays open until the last person has walked through, then shuts behind everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门一直开着，直到最后一个人走过，才在所有人身后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt with no line left for extras, because every cost was written inside the total.
abstract.cn: 想象一张账单，没有任何一行留给额外费用，因为每项成本都已写进总数。

examples.en: The library runs an inclusive reading hour for children of every ability.
examples.cn: 图书馆为各种能力的孩子开设包容性阅读时段。

examples.en: The fare is inclusive of taxes, so the final bill will not change.
examples.cn: 票价已含税，因此最终账单不会再变。

examples.en: Count the seats from the first row to the fifth inclusive.
examples.cn: 座位从第一排数到第五排，含首尾两排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里面」加「关」——先把所有人都关进圈内，再合上门 → 包容的、包括在内的

root: inclusive 来自中世纪拉丁 inclusivus，再往上出自拉丁 includere「关在里面」= in-「在内」+ claudere「关闭」。claudere 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定；与 clavis「钥匙」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a boundary is drawn so that nothing and nobody is left outside. The line is applied to a group, a price, a range, a wording, a classroom, an economy and finally to the grammar of who counts as 'we'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条线展开：画一条边界，使任何人与任何事物都不被留在外面。这条线依次用于群体、价格、范围、措辞、课堂、经济，最后用于「我们」是否包括听者的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of chairs with its last gap filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈椅子，最后一个缺口也被补上。

branches.en: THE CLOSED CIRCLE: the first sense fills the last empty chair so that no group stays outside.
branches.cn: 闭合的圆圈：第一个义项补上最后一把空椅，使任何群体都不留在外面。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a total or a range counts what lies inside, including both ends.
branches.cn: 线本身：总数或范围只计入线内之物，两端也包括在内。

branches.en: THE SEALED PRICE: every cost is written inside the total, leaving nothing to bill later.
branches.cn: 封住的价格：每项成本都写进总数，事后不再收费。

branches.en: ROOM IN THE SENTENCE AND THE CLASS: wording and schooling must also leave a chair for everyone.
branches.cn: 句子与教室里的位置：措辞与教育同样必须给每个人留一把椅子。

branches.en: GAIN AND GRAMMAR: prosperity reaches the margin, and the pronoun keeps the listener inside the circle.
branches.cn: 收益与语法：繁荣抵达边缘，代词把听者留在圈内。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin prefix meaning 'in', a Latin verb for shutting, a medieval adjective ending and the derived words built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示「在内」的拉丁前缀、表示关闭的拉丁动词、中世纪形容词后缀以及同一词干上的派生词逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- and claudere together give include and the whole family; the adjective ending -ive marks a quality, and -ity turns it into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 与 claudere 合成 include 与整个词族；形容词后缀标记性质，名词后缀再把它变成名词。

items.example: The prefix places the action inside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放进一条边界之内。

items.structure: claudere, clausi, clausum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The Latin verb supplies the closing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供「关闭」的意象。

items.meaning: to shut in; to count as part of a group
the act or state of being included
items.example: The inclusion of new voices changed the report.
items.exampleCN: 新声音的加入改变了这份报告。

items.meaning: tending to include; leaving nothing out
items.meaningCN: 倾向于包含的；不遗漏的
items.example: The policy is inclusive of part-time workers.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策把兼职工作者也包括在内。

items.example: The list was read inclusively, from the first name to the last.
items.exampleCN: 名单从第一个名字读到最后，首尾都算在内。

items.example: Reviewers praised the inclusiveness of the design.
items.exampleCN: 评审者称赞这项设计的包容性。

items.meaningCN: 有意识地接纳所有群体的做法
items.example: The agency published targets for inclusivity.
items.exampleCN: 该机构公布了包容性目标。

items.example: Breakfast is included in the room rate.
The ending turns a verb into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成描述性词语。

derivatives.meaning: to take in as part of a whole
the act or state of being included
in a way that leaves nothing out
the quality of being open to all

definition_zh: 已驯化的；家养的；栽培的；安于家庭生活的
definition_en: tamed and kept by people, or adapted to household life
core_image: 一只狗不挖洞、不守食，只在炉边等一只手落下，皮毛上的斑块是几代人挑出来的
scene: 院里的狗不再冲着陌生人叫， The domesticated dog sleeps by the stove instead of digging a den.
sceneCN: 这里 domesticated 指「已被人类驯养、依赖人的」（第 1 个义项：动物已家养化）；句意为这只家养的狗睡在炉边，而不再去挖洞穴。图中可辨识物件：炉边草垫、蜷睡的狗、没有掘土的爪、屋门。

pos.zh: 已驯化的；家养的；栽培的；安于家居的

senses.title: An animal tamed and kept
senses.definition: describing an animal that has been tamed and lives under human care
senses.definitionCN: 形容已被驯服、生活在人类照料下的动物
senses.example: The domesticated herd returns to the same pen every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这群家养牲畜每晚回到同一个圈里。
senses.why: the participle reports a finished change, so the animal is described by what has already happened to its line.
senses.whyCN: 分词报告一个已完成的变化，因此这只动物是由其谱系已经历的事来描述的。

senses.title: A plant brought into cultivation
senses.definition: describing a plant that depends on sowing and tending by people
senses.definitionCN: 形容依赖人类播种与照料的植物
senses.example: The domesticated wheat has a brittle-free rachis that keeps the ear intact.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培小麦的穗轴不易折断，使整穗保持完整。
senses.why: the same participle covers plants, because cultivation is the botanical form of keeping something in the house.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词也覆盖植物，因为栽培是「养在屋里」在植物学上的形式。

senses.title: Genetically adapted to people
senses.definition: describing inherited traits that fit a species to human environments
senses.definitionCN: 形容使物种适应人类环境的可遗传性状
senses.example: The domesticated strain digests starch more easily than its wild cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培品系比野生近亲更容易消化淀粉。
senses.why: once selection is repeated across generations, the adaptation sits in the genes and can be described as a state.
senses.whyCN: 当选择跨代重复，适应便落在基因里，可以被描述为一种状态。

senses.title: A person settled into home life
senses.definition: describing a person who has grown used to domestic routines and indoor comfort
senses.definitionCN: 形容已习惯于家庭日常与室内舒适的人
senses.example: He became domesticated after two winters of desk work.
senses.exampleCN: 两冬的案头工作之后，他变得安于家居。
senses.why: the animal image turns on people with a mild irony: home has tamed them too.
senses.whyCN: 动物的意象带着淡淡反讽转到人身上：家也把他们驯服了。

senses.title: Made tame or harmless
senses.definition: figuratively, describing something once dangerous or wild that has been made safe
senses.definitionCN: 比喻形容曾经危险或野性之物已被变得安全
senses.example: The domesticated storm scene lost its violence in the film version.
senses.exampleCN: 在电影版本里，那场被驯化的暴风雨失去了暴烈。
senses.why: if a beast can be domesticated, so can an image, a style or an argument.
senses.whyCN: 兽可以被驯化，意象、风格或论点也可以。

senses.title: Land brought under settled use
senses.titleCN: 被纳入定居经营的土地
senses.definition: describing a landscape converted to fields, terraces or managed pasture
senses.definitionCN: 形容已被改为田地、梯田或管理牧场的景观
senses.example: The domesticated slope holds soil that the wild slope lost.
senses.exampleCN: 被驯化的坡面留住了野坡已经流失的土。
senses.why: a landscape can be described by the same participle because it has been brought into the human household.
senses.whyCN: 景观也能用同一个分词描述，因为它已被带进人类的家户。

senses.title: A treaty incorporated into domestic law
senses.definition: in law, describing an international agreement given effect in national law
senses.definitionCN: 法律上形容已在国家法中生效的国际协定
senses.example: The domesticated convention can now be cited in national courts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份已国内法化的公约如今可在本国法院援引。
senses.why: the legal participle repeats the household image: the text has been moved inside.
senses.whyCN: 法律分词重复了家户意象：文本已被搬进屋内。

senses.title: House-trained in informal use
senses.definition: informal, describing a person or animal that behaves well indoors
senses.definitionCN: 口语形容在人前或室内举止得体的
senses.example: The puppy is domesticated enough to sleep indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 这只小狗已经规矩到可以睡在屋里了。
senses.why: the oldest household sense survives as a joke about indoor manners.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的家户义以关于室内举止的玩笑方式留存下来。

intro.en: Domesticated is the past participle of domesticate, from Latin domesticare, built on domus 'house'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domesticated 是 domesticate 的过去分词，动词出自拉丁 domesticare，建于 domus「房子」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus meant 'house, household'; its pre-Latin base is reconstructed, and the link to a building root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: domus 意为「房子、家户」；其拉丁语之前的词基属重构，与「建造」词根的联系只是假说。

items.en: Domesticus 'of the household' described people, animals and objects belonging to a house.
items.cn: domesticus「属于家户的」可描述属于一户的人、动物与物件。

items.en: Domesticare 'to make domestic, tame' supplied the English verb and therefore this participle.
items.cn: domesticare「使家用、使驯服」提供英语动词，因而也提供这个分词。

items.en: The English participle domesticated is recorded from the seventeenth century, first of animals.
items.cn: 英语分词 domesticated 自 17 世纪有记录，最初用于动物。

items.en: Later it described plants, people, landscapes and treaties; the informal house-trained sense is nineteenth-century and its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 后来它描述植物、人、景观与条约；口语「规矩」义属 19 世纪，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group is the same household family in adjective form; the second lists adjectives for organisms or people under human control.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个「家户」词族的形容词形态；第二组是形容受人类控制的生物或人的形容词。

entries.definition: Of the home in general; a domestic cat is kept indoors, but domestic also covers chores, flights and politics.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指家庭的；家猫是养在屋内的，但 domestic 也用于家务、航班与政治。

entries.definition: The act of taming; the participle describes the result of that act.
entries.definitionCN: 指驯化的动作；分词描述该动作的结果。

entries.definition: The long historical process; the participle is the state at the end of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指漫长的历史过程；分词是过程终点的状态。

entries.definition: The quality of home life; it does not describe tamed animals.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭生活的性质；不形容被驯化的动物。

entries.definition: Describing an animal that is not afraid of people; it can be true of one individual and need not be inherited.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不怕人的动物；可以只对个体成立，不必可遗传。

entries.definition: Describing land or plants that are tended; it stresses labour rather than inherited change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容受照料的地或植物；强调劳动，而非可遗传的改变。

entries.definition: Belonging to a home as a social unit; it names the unit, not the tamed condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为社会单位的家庭；指单位，而非被驯化的状态。

entries.definition: Describing a species established in a new region; it may be wild there and still be called naturalized.
entries.definitionCN: 形容在新地区立足的物种；在那里可能仍是野生的，却也称 naturalized。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the participle ending, the household core and the nouns it most often modifies.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：分词词尾、家户核心，以及它最常修饰的名词。

normal.en: domesticate + -ed = the state after taming, as in a domesticated breed.
normal.cn: domesticate + -ed = 驯化之后的状态，如家养品种。

normal.en: The word often sits before animals, plants, breeds and forms.
normal.cn: 这个词常放在 animals、plants、breeds、forms 之前。

normal.en: The base domus 'house' explains why the word also means house-trained.
normal.cn: 词基 domus「房子」解释了它为什么也有「屋内规矩」的意思。

normal.en: Compare the chain: domesticate, domesticated, domestication.
normal.cn: 比较这条链：domesticate、domesticated、domestication。

normal.en: The adjective is gradable: more domesticated, most domesticated.
normal.cn: 这个形容词可分级，可以说「更驯化」「最驯化」。

abstract.en: Picture a paw that has forgotten how to dig.
abstract.cn: 想象一只爪子，已经忘了怎么刨土。

abstract.en: Picture a coat with patches that were chosen by people, not by weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一身斑块毛色，是人挑出来的，而不是天气挑的。

abstract.en: Picture a field whose soil stays put because a wall was built for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片田，土不再流失，因为有人为它砌了墙。

examples.en: Domesticated animals usually have smaller teeth than their wild relatives.
examples.cn: 家养动物的牙通常比野生近亲更小。

examples.en: The domesticated varieties ripen together, which suits machine harvest.
examples.cn: 栽培品种同时成熟，适合机械收割。

examples.en: After a year indoors he had become thoroughly domesticated.
examples.cn: 在室内待了一年后，他已完全安于家居生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多麦斯提凯提德」后半的「提德」听成「提进屋的」——已经被提进屋、喂熟了的，就是已驯化的。

root: 动词 domesticate 出自拉丁 domesticare「使家用、使驯服」，其基础是 domus「房子、家户」所生的 domesticus。过去分词 -ed 表示「已处于该状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe results: tamed animals, cultivated plants, genetic adaptation, settled people, harmless versions of wild things, managed land, incorporated treaties and indoor manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述结果：家养动物、栽培植物、遗传适应、安于家居的人、被磨平的野性、被经营的土地、已纳入的条约、室内举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog asleep by the stove with paws that no longer dig.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只狗睡在炉边，爪子已不再刨土。

branches.en: ANIMAL AND GENES: the tame individual and the adapted line are the same result at two depths.
branches.cn: 动物与基因：温顺的个体与适应的谱系，是同一结果的两个深度。

branches.en: PLANT: cultivation produces a plant that cannot sow itself.
branches.cn: 植物：栽培产生一种无法自行播种的植物。

branches.en: PERSON AND MANNERS: a settled adult and a house-trained puppy share the household image.
branches.cn: 人与举止：安于家居的成年人与守规矩的幼犬共享家户意象。

branches.en: SOFTENED WILDNESS: images and styles can be made harmless too.
branches.cn: 被磨平的野性：意象与风格也可以被变得无害。

branches.en: GROUND AND LAW: a slope and a treaty are both brought inside a managed order.
branches.cn: 土地与法律：坡地与条约都被带进一种受管理的秩序。

intro.en: Domesticated is a Latin household verb with an English past-participle ending used as an adjective.
intro.cn: domesticated 是拉丁「家户」动词加英语过去分词词尾，并作形容词使用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base domus also yields domicile and domestic; the tame verb domare is a separate root and only looks related.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 domus 还衍生 domicile 与 domestic；表驯服的 domare 属另一词根，只是看起来相关。

items.example: The stem explains the indoor sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干解释了「屋内」义。

items.example: The adjective supplies the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供动词的基础。

items.example: The ending reports a completed change.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾报告已完成的变化。

items.example: Domesticated bees are kept in hives.

items.exampleCN: 半驯化的驯鹿仍会迁徙。

definition_zh: 宇宙学的；与宇宙整体尺度及其演化有关的
definition_en: relating to cosmology or to the universe considered on its largest scales
core_image: 一把量到星系际距离的尺子，刻度以亿光年为单位
scene: 天文学课堂上，教师在黑板上画出随距离增大的红移曲线，标出对应的距离刻度。 The cosmological redshift is treated as a stretching of space rather than motion through it.
sceneCN: 这里指「与宇宙整体尺度及其演化有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于宇宙学范围的）；句意为宇宙学红移被理解为空间的拉伸，而不是在空间中的运动。图中可辨识物件：黑板曲线、坐标轴、红移标记、粉笔。

pos.zh: 宇宙学的；宇宙整体尺度的

senses.title: Relating to cosmology
senses.definition: belonging to or studied within cosmology
senses.definitionCN: 属于宇宙学或在宇宙学范围内研究的
senses.example: The paper sits at the cosmological end of astrophysics.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文位于天体物理学的宇宙学一端。
senses.why: -ical turns the noun cosmology into the adjective of relation, so the word simply means 'of cosmology'.
senses.whyCN: -ical 把名词 cosmology 变成表关系的形容词，因此这个词就是「宇宙学的」。

senses.title: Cosmological redshift
senses.definition: the redshift produced by the expansion of space during the light's journey
senses.definitionCN: 光在旅途中因空间膨胀而产生的红移
senses.example: The cosmological redshift is treated as a stretching of space rather than motion through it.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学红移被理解为空间的拉伸，而不是在空间中的运动。
senses.why: the adjective marks the cause: expansion of the whole, not local motion of a source.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记成因：整体空间的膨胀，而非光源的局部运动。

senses.title: Cosmological distance
senses.definition: a distance defined with the expansion of the universe taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 把宇宙膨胀计入其中而定义的距离
senses.example: Cosmological distance is not a single number but a family of measures.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学距离不是一个单一数值，而是一组测量。
senses.why: expanding space makes ordinary distance ambiguous, so the adjective marks a distance defined on the cosmic model.
senses.whyCN: 空间膨胀使普通距离含混，因此形容词标记一种在宇宙模型上定义的距离。

senses.title: Cosmological constant
senses.definition: the constant term Einstein added to his equations, now identified with dark energy
senses.definitionCN: 爱因斯坦加入方程的那个常数项，如今与暗能量相联系
senses.example: The cosmological constant is measured to be very small but not zero.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学常数被测得极小，但不为零。
senses.why: the adjective fixes the constant as one belonging to the equations of the whole universe.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把这个常数限定为属于整个宇宙方程的那一个。

senses.title: Cosmological model
senses.definition: a mathematical description of the universe's geometry and history
senses.definitionCN: 对宇宙几何与历史的数学描述
senses.example: Each cosmological model predicts a different expansion history.
senses.exampleCN: 每个宇宙学模型都预言不同的膨胀史。
senses.why: the adjective distinguishes models of the whole from models of a single object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把整体模型与单个天体的模型区分开。

senses.title: Cosmological time scale
senses.definition: a span of time comparable with the age of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 可与宇宙年龄相比的时间跨度
senses.example: On a cosmological time scale, a century is invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 在宇宙学时间尺度上，一个世纪根本看不见。
senses.why: the adjective rescales time to the whole history rather than to human experience.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把时间重新标度到整段历史，而非人类经验。

senses.title: Cosmological principle
senses.definition: the assumption that on large scales the universe is homogeneous and isotropic
senses.definitionCN: 假设宇宙在极大尺度上是均匀且各向同性的
senses.example: The cosmological principle lets one model describe the whole sky.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学原理使一个模型足以描述整片天空。
senses.why: a principle about the whole deserves the adjective, since it is assumed before any local measurement.
senses.whyCN: 关于整体的原理理应用这个形容词，因为它在任何局部测量之前就被假设。

senses.title: Figurative vast in scale
senses.definition: a borrowed use for anything measured on an enormous scale
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何以极大尺度衡量的事物
senses.example: The company's failure was cosmological in its own small universe.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的失败在它自己的小宇宙里是宇宙级的。
senses.why: the largest available scale became an intensifier for scale itself.
senses.whyCN: 可用的最大尺度成了「尺度」本身的加强语。

intro.en: Cosmological is cosmology plus the relational suffix -ical, from Greek kosmos and -logia through Latinized forms. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cosmological 是 cosmology 加表关系的后缀 -ical，源于希腊 kosmos 与 -logia 的拉丁化形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant 'order' and then 'the ordered world'; its deeper origin is unsettled.
items.cn: kosmos 意为「秩序」，后指「有序的世界」；其更深来源无定论。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' produced cosmology through Latinized cosmologia in the early modern period.
items.cn: -logia「论述、研究」在近代早期经拉丁化 cosmologia 产生 cosmology。

items.en: The relational suffix -ical came through Latin -icalis and French -ique, and turns the noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.cn: 表关系的后缀 -ical 经拉丁 -icalis 与法语 -ique 而来，把名词变成表归属的形容词。

items.en: The cosmological constant entered physics with Einstein's 1917 paper on the universe as a whole.
items.cn: 宇宙学常数随爱因斯坦 1917 年关于整体宇宙的论文进入物理学。

items.en: Twentieth-century cosmology multiplied fixed phrases such as cosmological redshift, distance and principle.
items.cn: 二十世纪的宇宙学衍生出宇宙学红移、宇宙学距离、宇宙学原理等大量固定短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Greek source of kosmos is unknown, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：kosmos 在希腊语之前的来源不明，常为其提出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike adjectives built on the same stem; group two holds near-meaning scale words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形近形容词；第二组是语义相近的尺度词。

entries.definition: A specific term in the equations; the adjective alone does not name that term.
entries.definitionCN: 方程中的特定术语；单用形容词并不指这个术语。

entries.definition: Formed by cosmic rays in the atmosphere or in rock, a different compound with -genic.
entries.definitionCN: 由宇宙射线在大气或岩石中生成的，是带 -genic 的另一个复合词。

entries.tag: of space not of the study
entries.definition: Belonging to outer space generally; cosmological specifically refers to the universe as a modelled whole.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于外层空间的；cosmological 特指作为被建模整体的宇宙。

entries.definition: Built on kosmos plus polites 'citizen': worldly and international, not cosmological at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kosmos 加 polites「公民」构成：世界性的、国际的，与宇宙学无关。

entries.definition: Applying to everything without exception; cosmological describes the universe as an object of study.
entries.definitionCN: 无例外地适用于一切；cosmological 描述作为研究对象的宇宙。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of stars and galaxies rather than the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 与恒星和星系的物理有关，而非整个宇宙。

entries.definition: Relating to planets; it marks a much smaller scale than the cosmological one.
entries.definitionCN: 与行星有关；其尺度远小于宇宙学尺度。

entries.definition: Covering a whole system or planet; it is a general word for totality, not a cosmic term.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个系统或行星；是表示整体的普通词，并非宇宙术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀与真实固定短语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Cosmology plus -ical makes the adjective of relation.
normal.cn: cosmology 加 -ical 构成表关系的形容词。

normal.en: The cosmological principle assumes the same physics everywhere on large scales.
normal.cn: 宇宙学原理假设极大尺度上处处物理相同。

normal.en: Cosmological redshift comes from stretched space, not from local motion.
normal.cn: 宇宙学红移来自被拉伸的空间，而非局部运动。

normal.en: The cosmological constant is now tied to dark energy.
normal.cn: 宇宙学常数如今与暗能量相联系。

normal.en: Cosmic means space in general; cosmological means the modelled whole.
normal.cn: cosmic 泛指太空；cosmological 指被建模的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks are counted in billions of light years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺，刻度以十亿光年计。

abstract.en: Picture a curve on a blackboard that rises with distance.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上一条随距离上升的曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a failure so large that it fills a small private universe.
abstract.cn: 想象一次大到填满私人小宇宙的失败。

examples.en: Cosmological measurements now constrain the age of the universe.
examples.cn: 宇宙学测量如今约束着宇宙年龄。

examples.en: The cosmological constant remains one of physics' deepest puzzles.
examples.cn: 宇宙学常数仍是物理学最深的谜题之一。

examples.en: On a cosmological scale, the whole human record is a brief flicker.
examples.cn: 在宇宙尺度上，整个人类记录只是一闪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cosmology（宇宙学）+ -ical（……的）」——属于宇宙学的、宇宙整体尺度的

root: cosmology + -ical；cosmology 来自希腊 kosmos「秩序、有序世界」+ -logia「研究」，经拉丁化 cosmologia；kosmos 更深来源不确定，其词根一说属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relational adjective: it marks the discipline, then redshift, distance, a constant, a model, a time scale, a principle and finally any enormous scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个关系形容词：它标记学科，继而标记红移、距离、常数、模型、时间尺度、原理，最后是任何巨大尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler graduated in billions of light years laid across a blackboard curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把以十亿光年为刻度的尺，横放在黑板上的曲线旁。

branches.en: RELATION AND INTENSITY: from 'of cosmology' to 'vast beyond measure'.
branches.cn: 关系与强度：从「属于宇宙学」到「大到无法量」。

branches.en: REDSHIFT: the adjective marks expansion as the cause.
branches.cn: 红移：形容词标记膨胀为成因。

branches.en: DISTANCE AND TIME: both are rescaled to the whole history.
branches.cn: 距离与时间：两者都被重新标度到整段历史。

branches.en: CONSTANT: a term fixed inside the equations of the whole.
branches.cn: 常数：固定在整体方程里的一个项。

branches.en: MODEL AND PRINCIPLE: the framework and the assumption beneath it.
branches.cn: 模型与原理：框架，以及它底下的假设。

intro.en: Cosmological is a derived adjective: a Greek compound noun plus a Latin-French relational suffix.
intro.cn: cosmological 是派生形容词：一个希腊复合名词加一个拉丁—法语来源的关系后缀。

latinIntro.en: Cosmologia and cosmos are the Latinized forms; -icalis supplies the adjective ending that English renders as -ical.
latinIntro.cn: cosmologia 与 cosmos 是拉丁化形式；-icalis 提供形容词词尾，英语作 -ical。

items.meaning: study of the universe as a whole

items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.meaning: from a cosmological point of view
items.exampleCN: 从宇宙学角度看，这一事件很近。

items.example: The cosmos is the object studied.

items.exampleCN: 宇成同位素在岩石中形成。
