cosmologia, cosmologiae (f., first declension, New Latin)

definition_zh: 工程科学；支撑工程设计的那部分科学知识，如力学、材料与传热
definition_en: the body of scientific knowledge, such as mechanics, materials and heat transfer, that supports engineering design
core_image: 黑板上左边是公式，右边是折断的试件，中间用一支粉笔画出两者的对应关系
scene: 黑板左边写满公式，右边摆着一段折断的试件，中间用粉笔画出二者的对应关系。 Engineering science explains why the beam bent before anyone tested it.
sceneCN: 这里 engineering science 指支撑工程设计的那部分科学知识（第 1 个义项：知识体系）；句意：工程科学在任何人做测试之前就解释了那根梁为什么会弯。

pos.zh: 工程科学；工程科学学科（作定语）

senses.title: The scientific base of design
senses.titleCN: 设计所依赖的科学基础
senses.definition: the knowledge of how materials, forces and flows behave that designers must rely on
senses.definitionCN: 设计者必须依赖的、关于材料、力与流动如何表现的知识
senses.example: Engineering science tells you the limit before the drawing is finished.
senses.exampleCN: 工程科学在图纸画完之前就告诉你极限在哪里。
senses.why: the compound joins a practice to the knowledge under it, so it names that knowledge first.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把实践与其底下的知识连在一起，因此首先指那套知识。

senses.title: A university department and degree
senses.definition: an academic unit or programme that teaches the theoretical side of engineering
senses.definitionCN: 讲授工程理论侧面的学术单位或培养项目
senses.example: The engineering science department shares a building with physics.
senses.exampleCN: 工程科学系与物理系共用一栋楼。
senses.why: a body of knowledge taught in one place becomes a department with a name.
senses.whyCN: 在一处讲授的知识体系会变成一个有名目的院系。

senses.title: Applied physics in practice
senses.definition: the working combination of mechanics, thermodynamics and materials knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 力学、热力学与材料知识的实际组合
senses.example: Engineering science here means heat, stress and fatigue in one course.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的工程科学指把热、应力与疲劳放在一门课里。
senses.why: the field is applied physics assembled around design problems rather than around nature alone.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问是把物理围绕设计问题、而不是围绕自然本身组装起来的。

senses.title: A subject in a curriculum
senses.definition: the taught course that gives students the theory behind their later projects
senses.definitionCN: 在学生日后做项目之前提供理论的讲授科目
senses.example: Engineering science is the second-year course everyone struggles with.
senses.exampleCN: 工程科学是二年级那门人人都吃力的课。
senses.why: the same content appears in a timetable, and the phrase becomes a course title.
senses.whyCN: 同样的内容出现在课表里，短语就成课程名称。

senses.title: Modelling and research work
senses.definition: the research activity of building and testing models of physical behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 建立并检验物理行为模型的研究活动
senses.example: Their engineering science produced a model that matched the test data.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的工程科学研究做出了与试验数据吻合的模型。
senses.why: between theory and test sits modelling, and the compound also names that activity.
senses.whyCN: 理论与试验之间是建模，这个复合词也指这项活动。

senses.title: The bridge between pure and applied
senses.titleCN: 纯科学与应用之间的桥梁
senses.definition: the middle ground that turns a physical result into a design rule
senses.definitionCN: 把物理结论转化为设计规则的中间地带
senses.example: Engineering science is where a physicist's result becomes a builder's rule.
senses.exampleCN: 工程科学就是物理学家的结论变成建造者规则的地方。
senses.why: the phrase exists precisely because neither pure science nor practice covers that middle step.
senses.whyCN: 正因为纯科学与实践都不覆盖这个中间步骤，这个短语才存在。

senses.title: Simulation and computation
senses.definition: the numerical study of behaviour by solving physical equations on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上求解物理方程以研究行为的数值工作
senses.example: Engineering science now spends more time on simulation than on hand calculation.
senses.exampleCN: 如今工程科学花在仿真上的时间比手算更多。
senses.why: once equations are solved by machine, modelling becomes a large part of the field.
senses.whyCN: 方程一旦由机器求解，建模就成为该领域的一大部分。

senses.title: A qualification area
senses.titleCN: 资格认证所对应的领域
senses.definition: the knowledge area examined when a technical qualification is awarded
senses.definitionCN: 授予技术资格时所考核的知识领域
senses.example: The exam covers engineering science before it covers project practice.
senses.exampleCN: 考试先考工程科学，再考项目实务。
senses.why: what a profession requires of newcomers is written into examinations, and the field is named there.
senses.whyCN: 行业对新人的要求会写进考试，领域名称也出现在那里。

intro.en: Engineering science joins a word for planned building with a Latin word for knowledge. The compound marks the point where knowing and making are deliberately separated for study.
intro.cn: engineering science 把「有计划的建造」与拉丁语「知识」拼在一起。这个复合词标记了「知」与「造」被刻意分开研究的那一点。

items.en: Latin ingenium gave English engine and then engineer, the person whose work became engineering.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 先给英语 engine，再给 engineer，这个人的工作后来成了 engineering。

items.en: From the eighteenth century engineering named the profession of roads, canals and machines.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，engineering 指道路、运河与机器这一行。

items.en: Latin scientia meant knowledge, from scire, to know. English science narrowed it to organised knowledge of the natural world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scientia 意为「知识」，来自 scire「知道」。英语 science 把它收窄为关于自然界的系统知识。

items.en: Engineering schools separated the underlying theory from workshop practice, and the union of the two words named that theory.
items.cn: 工程学校把底层理论与车间实务分开，两个词的联合就指那套理论。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase covered mechanics, materials, fluids and heat as a single teaching and research field.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个短语把力学、材料、流体与传热合为一个教学与研究领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of Latin scire is debated, and the forms sometimes derived for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语 scire 更早的来源有争论，为它推导出的形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group shares the words inside the compound; the second group is neighbouring names for knowledge about made things.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合词内部的词；第二组是关于人造物的相邻知识名称。

entries.definition: The profession itself; engineering science is the theory that the profession applies.
entries.definitionCN: 指职业本身；engineering science 是该职业所应用的理论。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge of nature; joined to engineering it is knowledge selected for design.
entries.definitionCN: 关于自然的系统知识；与 engineering 组合后，指为设计而选取的知识。

entries.definition: Science aimed at practical problems; the compound is the engineering school's name for that aim.
entries.definitionCN: 面向实际问题的科学；这个复合词是工程院校对该取向的称呼。

entries.definition: The hands-on side of technical education, as opposed to the theoretical side named here.
entries.definitionCN: 技术教育中偏动手的一面，与这里命名的理论一面相对。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion; it is the oldest and largest part of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学问；是该领域最古老、最大的一块。

entries.definition: The study of how substances behave under load, heat and time.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质在受力、受热与时间作用下如何表现。

entries.definition: The study of matter and energy as such; the compound selects from it what design needs.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量本身；复合词从中挑出设计所需的部分。

entries.definition: The decisions that turn this knowledge into a particular object.
entries.definitionCN: 把这类知识变成具体对象的那些决定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the two real words and the real academic phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自两个真实词与真实学术搭配。

normal.en: Scientia is knowledge, so the phrase is literally the knowledge under the building trade.
normal.cn: scientia 是知识，所以这个短语字面上就是「建造行业底下的知识」。

normal.en: Engine goes back to ingenium, inborn talent, so the whole phrase runs from talent to knowledge.
normal.cn: engine 可追到 ingenium「天生才能」，整个短语从才能一路走到知识。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: engineering science course, engineering science department.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：工程科学课程、工程科学系。

normal.en: It is the middle term: not pure physics, not workshop practice.
normal.cn: 它是中间项：既不是纯物理，也不是车间实务。

normal.en: Three contents anchor it: mechanics, materials, heat.
normal.cn: 三项内容锚定它：力学、材料、热。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line drawn between an equation and a broken test piece.
abstract.cn: 想象在一条公式与一段折断的试件之间画着一道粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book whose pages are printed in the language of physics.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，书页是用物理的语言印的。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that exists first as a set of assumptions.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，最初只是一组假设。

examples.en: Engineering science predicts failure; inspection only finds it.
examples.cn: 工程科学预测失效，检验只是把它找出来。

examples.en: The department changed its name from engineering science to mechanical engineering.
examples.cn: 那个系把名字从工程科学改成了机械工程。

examples.en: Students learn engineering science before they learn to trust a simulation.
examples.cn: 学生先学工程科学，才学会信任仿真结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩机捏 ring（engineering）赛恩斯（science）」——工程背后那套赛过直觉的学问，就是工程科学

root: 拉丁 ingenium「天生才能」→ engine / engineer → engineering；拉丁 scientia「知识」← scire「知道」→ science；十九世纪工程院校把底层理论从车间实务中分出，合成 engineering science。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the knowledge base, a department, applied physics, a course, modelling research, the middle ground, simulation and a qualification area.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖知识基础、院系、应用物理、课程、建模研究、中间地带、仿真与资格领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard with equations on one side and a broken specimen on the other, joined by a chalk line.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板一边是公式，一边是折断的试件，中间由一道粉笔线相连。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND ITS ROLE: the supporting body of knowledge, and its position between physics and building.
branches.cn: 知识及其位置：作为支撑的知识体系，以及它处于物理与建造之间的位置。

branches.en: TAUGHT FORM: a department with a building, and a course on a timetable.
branches.cn: 教学形态：有楼宇的院系，以及课表上的一门课。

branches.en: CONTENT AND COMPUTATION: mechanics with heat and materials, and the simulation that now carries much of it.
branches.cn: 内容与计算：力学连同热与材料，以及如今承载其中许多工作的仿真。

branches.en: MODELLING RESEARCH: building and checking models against test data.
branches.cn: 建模研究：建立模型并用试验数据检验。

branches.en: QUALIFICATION: the examined knowledge area for a technical title.
branches.cn: 资格：技术头衔所考核的知识领域。

intro.en: Engineering science is two nouns side by side. Neither half takes a new affix, but each already carries its own endings.
intro.cn: engineering science 是两个名词并置而成。两半都没有新增词缀，但各自已带原有词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ingenium behind engine, and scientia behind science; the English endings -ing and -ence were added before the nouns met.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 engine 背后的 ingenium 与 science 背后的 scientia；英语词尾 -ing 与 -ence 在两词相遇前就已加上。

items.example: It belongs to the Latin noun behind engine.
items.exampleCN: 它属于 engine 背后的那个拉丁名词。

items.example: The verb explains the sense of something produced.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词解释了「被产出之物」的含义。

items.example: The ending turns the builder into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把建造者变成一门职业。

items.example: The verb is the source of the second noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是第二个名词的来源。
这个名词指系统化的知识。

items.example: The ending shapes the English noun science.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾塑成英语名词 science。

items.example: The ending appears in the related adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾出现在相关形容词中。

items.example: The person-word sits between engine and engineering.
items.exampleCN: 人物名词处在 engine 与 engineering 之间。

definition_zh: 着色；色彩；体色；（生物的）色彩图案
definition_en: the arrangement or quality of colours on an organism or object, or the act of giving something colour
core_image: 一只甲虫的鞘翅从深蓝过渡到金属绿，颜色像被刷上去的一层
scene: 热带雨林的落叶层上，一只甲虫的鞘翅随角度由深蓝转为金属绿。 The beetle's iridescent coloration warns birds that it tastes bitter.
sceneCN: 这里 coloration 指「生物体表的整体色彩图案」（第 1 个义项：一个生物身上颜色的分布与组合方式）；句意为这只甲虫彩虹般的体色警告鸟类它味道苦涩。图中可辨识物件：甲虫鞘翅、蓝绿渐变、退开的鸟。

pos.zh: 着色；色彩；体色；色彩图案（多不可数）

senses.title: Overall colour pattern of an organism
senses.titleCN: 生物体表的整体色彩图案
senses.definition: the whole arrangement of colours and markings on an animal's or plant's body
senses.definitionCN: 动物或植物身上颜色与斑纹的整体分布
senses.example: The beetle's iridescent coloration warns birds that it tastes bitter.
senses.exampleCN: 这只甲虫的虹彩体色警告鸟类它味道苦涩。
senses.why: The -ation noun names the resulting state: what the colours together look like on a body.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词命名结果状态：各种颜色在体表合起来呈现的样子。

senses.title: Cryptic coloration
senses.definition: colours that match the background and make an animal difficult to see
senses.definitionCN: 与背景相合、使动物难以被看见的颜色
senses.example: The lizard's cryptic coloration makes it disappear against the gravel.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蜥蜴的隐蔽色使它消失在砾石背景中。
senses.why: Hiding is the most common use of body colour, so the general noun took this sense early.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏是体色最常见的用途，因此这个一般名词很早就承担了这一义。

senses.title: Warning coloration
senses.definition: bright colours that advertise a defence such as poison or a sting
senses.definitionCN: 鲜艳的颜色，用以通告毒液或蜇针等防御手段
senses.example: The wasp's black and yellow coloration is a warning, not an invitation.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂的黑黄体色是警告，不是邀请。
senses.why: The same surface can carry the opposite message: instead of hiding, it announces.
senses.whyCN: 同一层体表可以传递相反的信息：不隐藏，而是宣告。

senses.title: Coloration of plants
senses.definition: the colours of leaves, flowers, fruits or stems, often serving attraction or protection
senses.definitionCN: 叶、花、果或茎的颜色，常起吸引或保护作用
senses.example: The red coloration of the fruit attracts seed-dispersing birds.
senses.exampleCN: 果实的红色吸引传播种子的鸟。
senses.why: Plants use colour for the same two jobs as animals: hide or advertise.
senses.whyCN: 植物用颜色做与动物同样的两件事：隐藏或宣传。

senses.title: Dyeing or colouring process
senses.definition: the act or process of giving colour to a material
senses.definitionCN: 给材料加上颜色的行为或过程
senses.example: The coloration of the glass takes place in a single furnace pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这块玻璃的着色在一次炉内处理中完成。
senses.why: The noun also names the act that produces the state, not only the state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也命名产生该状态的行为，而不只是状态本身。

senses.title: Colour scheme in design
senses.definition: the chosen combination of colours in a design, garment or interior
senses.definitionCN: 设计、服装或室内所选用的颜色组合
senses.example: The room's warm coloration makes it feel smaller and calmer.
senses.exampleCN: 房间的暖色调让它显得更小、更安静。
senses.why: The word extends from bodies to made objects once colour is planned as a scheme.
senses.whyCN: 一旦颜色被当作方案来规划，这个词就从身体扩展到人造物。

senses.title: Vocal coloration or timbre
senses.definition: the quality of tone that gives a voice or instrument its particular character
senses.definitionCN: 赋予人声或乐器特定性格的音质
senses.example: Her low coloration suits the narrator's quiet authority.
senses.exampleCN: 她低沉的音色正适合叙述者那种安静的权威感。
senses.why: Music borrows the visual word: timbre colours a sound the way pigment colours a surface.
senses.whyCN: 音乐借用了这个视觉词：音色给声音上色，正如颜料给表面上色。

senses.title: Slight bias in a report
senses.definition: a subtle emotional or political tint given to a description or account
senses.definitionCN: 给描述或叙述加上细微的情绪或政治色彩
senses.example: The report's cheerful coloration hides a serious failure.
senses.exampleCN: 报告欢快的色彩掩盖了一次严重失误。
senses.why: The figurative sense keeps the idea of a surface coat: wording adds a hue without changing the facts.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义保留「表面涂层」的意思：措辞加上一层色调，却不改变事实。

intro.en: Coloration comes from Latin colorare 'to colour', a verb built on color, through French coloration. The deeper origin of Latin color is debated; the common link to a root meaning 'to cover' is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: coloration 经法语 coloration 来自拉丁 colorare「着色」，后者由 color 构成。拉丁 color 的更早来源有争议；把它与表示「遮盖」的词根相联属重构。

items.en: Latin color meant 'colour, hue, outward appearance' and also 'pretext'; it is the noun behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁 color 意为「颜色、色调、外观」，也指「借口」；它是整族词背后的名词。

items.en: Colorare 'to give colour to, to dye' is a derivative verb of color, with coloratus as its participle.
items.cn: colorare「给……上色、染」是由 color 派生的动词，分词为 coloratus。

items.en: French coloration named the act or result of colouring and passed into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 coloration 命名着色行为或结果，16 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Biology fixed the sense 'body colour pattern' in the nineteenth century, when protective and warning coloration became standard terms.
items.cn: 生物学在 19 世纪固定了「体色图案」这一义，当时保护色与警戒色成为标准术语。

items.en: The musical and rhetorical senses are later metaphors: timbre and wording are treated as coats of colour.
items.cn: 音乐义与修辞义是更晚的比喻：音色与措辞都被当作一层颜色涂层。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): Latin color may descend from a root meaning 'to cover, conceal', which would also explain celare 'to hide'; this is a reconstruction and competing accounts exist. The first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：拉丁 color 可能出自表示「覆盖、隐藏」的词根，这也能解释 celare「藏」；此说属重构形式，另有不同说法。首见英语年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from its verb and adjective relatives; group two separates terms that describe colour in organisms, design and language.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与它的动词、形容词同族；第二组区分描述生物、设计与语言中颜色的术语。

entries.definition: A particular hue or the material producing it; coloration is the pattern or state produced.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一种色调或产生它的材料；coloration 指由此形成的图案或状态。

entries.definition: A dye or pigment added to something; it is an agent, not a resulting appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 指加入某物中的染料或颜料；是施动者，不是呈现出的外观。

entries.definition: Having colour; it states a property rather than naming the pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 表示有颜色；陈述一种属性，而不命名图案。

entries.definition: The same word in British spelling; American texts use coloration.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英式拼写；美式文本用 coloration。

entries.definition: Colour produced specifically by pigment in tissue; coloration is the broader visible pattern, however produced.
entries.definitionCN: 特指组织内色素产生的颜色；coloration 是更宽泛的可见图案，不问成因。

entries.definition: The act of adding colour or the added substance; coloration is more common in scientific description.
entries.definitionCN: 指加色的行为或所加物质；coloration 更常用于科学描述。

entries.definition: One shade within the spectrum; coloration covers the whole arrangement of shades.
entries.definitionCN: 指光谱中的单一色调；coloration 覆盖全部色调的组合。

entries.definition: Visible spots, stripes or patches; coloration includes both markings and the ground colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指可见的斑点、条纹或斑块；coloration 同时包含斑纹与底色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real scientific compounds, and the genuine extension into music and rhetoric.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的科学复合词，以及进入音乐与修辞的真实引申。

normal.en: color + -ation: the state or act of being coloured.
normal.cn: color 加 -ation：被上色的状态或行为。

normal.en: The family runs color, colorare, coloration, colorful, colorless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 color、colorare、coloration、colorful、colorless。

normal.en: Biology pairs the term with cryptic, protective and warning.
normal.cn: 生物学把这个词与 cryptic、protective、warning 搭配。

normal.en: Iridescent coloration changes with the angle of light.
normal.cn: 虹彩体色随光线角度变化。

normal.en: The same noun serves animals, paint, interiors and voices.
normal.cn: 同一个名词可用于动物、涂料、室内与嗓音。

abstract.en: Picture a beetle whose shell shifts from blue to green as it turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一只甲虫转身时鞘翅从蓝变绿。

abstract.en: Picture a warning flag painted on a living body.
abstract.cn: 想象一面警告旗被画在活体身上。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence wearing a cheerful coat over bad news.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话给坏消息披上欢快的外衣。

examples.en: Seasonal coloration helps the hare match snow and soil.
examples.cn: 季节性体色帮助野兔匹配雪地与泥土。

examples.en: The glass owes its green coloration to iron impurities.
examples.cn: 这块玻璃的绿色来自铁杂质。

examples.en: The choir's warm coloration softened the closing line.
examples.cn: 合唱团温暖的音色软化了收尾句。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「color（颜色）+ -ation（状态）」——呈现出来的颜色状态 → 色彩；体色

root: 拉丁 color「颜色、外观」→ 拉丁 colorare「着色」→ 法语 coloration → 英语 coloration；拉丁 color 的更深词根存疑，可能与表示「遮盖」的词根有关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one surface of colour: an organism's pattern, its hiding and warning uses, plants, dyeing, design, vocal timbre, and finally the tint of a report.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一层颜色表面长出：生物的图案、其隐藏与警告用途、植物、染色、设计、音色，最后是叙述的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beetle's wing case shifting from deep blue to metallic green as it turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只甲虫的鞘翅随转动从深蓝变为金属绿。

branches.en: BODY PATTERN: the whole arrangement of colour on an organism, including concealment.
branches.cn: 体表图案：生物身上颜色的整体安排，包括隐蔽。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND PLANT: colour advertises defence and draws pollinators or dispersers.
branches.cn: 信号与植物：颜色通告防御，也吸引传粉者或传播者。

branches.en: PROCESS: colour is applied to a material rather than grown on a body.
branches.cn: 过程：颜色被施加到材料上，而非长在身体上。

branches.en: DESIGN: colours are chosen as a deliberate scheme.
branches.cn: 设计：颜色被当作有意的方案来挑选。

branches.en: METAPHOR: tone colours a voice, and wording colours an account.
branches.cn: 比喻：音色给嗓音上色，措辞给叙述上色。

intro.en: Coloration is a Latin verb stem plus the noun ending -ation; the Latin family around color supplies verbs, adjectives and agent nouns.
intro.cn: coloration 是拉丁动词词干加名词词尾 -ation；围绕 color 的拉丁词族提供动词、形容词与施动名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin color, colorare and coloratus supply the stem and the sense of applying colour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 color、colorare 与 coloratus 提供词干及「施加颜色」的含义。

items.example: Color is the noun behind the family.
items.exampleCN: color 是整族词背后的名词。

items.example: The ending names both the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀同时命名行为与结果。

items.example: The bird's coloration is purely seasonal.
items.exampleCN: 这只鸟的体色完全是季节性的。

items.example: The reef is colorful at noon.
items.exampleCN: 正午时珊瑚礁色彩丰富。

items.example: The glass is colored with iron oxide.
items.exampleCN: 这块玻璃用氧化铁着色。

items.example: A natural colorant replaced the dye.
items.exampleCN: 一种天然着色剂取代了染料。
色度测量追踪甲虫的色调。

definition_zh: 海洋生物（生活在海洋中的任何生物个体或类群）
definition_en: any living thing that spends all or part of its life in the sea
core_image: 一只小小的甲壳类在咸水里张合附肢，身体里的盐分与周围海水不断交换
scene: 取样瓶里的一只小甲壳类在低温海水中仍缓慢活动。 A marine organism must cope with salt, cold and constant pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 marine organism 指「生活在海洋中的生物个体」（第 1 个义项：作为个体或类群的海洋生物）；句意为一种海洋生物必须应对盐分、低温与持续压力。

pos.zh: 海洋生物（可数，复数 marine organisms）

derivatives.zh: marinus（拉丁「海的」）→ 海洋的：与海有关的
organon（希腊「工具、器官」）+ -ismos（名词后缀）→ 生物体：由器官构成的有机整体
micro-（希腊「小」）+ organism（生物体）→ 微生物：肉眼不可见的生物
organon（器官）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ 有机的：与生命器官有关的
organon（希腊「工具、器官」经拉丁 organum 借入）→ 器官；机构

senses.title: Any sea-living thing
senses.titleCN: 海洋生物：生活在海中的任何生物
senses.definition: any organism whose habitat is the sea
senses.definitionCN: 以海洋为栖息环境的任何生物
senses.example: A marine organism must cope with salt, cold and constant pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 一种海洋生物必须应对盐分、低温与持续压力。
senses.why: marine fixes the habitat and organism fixes the living thing, so the phrase covers every sea-dwelling species.
senses.whyCN: marine 限定栖息地，organism 限定生物本身，短语因此涵盖所有海生物种。

senses.title: The planktonic kind
senses.definition: a small organism that drifts with currents rather than swimming against them
senses.definitionCN: 随水流漂移、不主动逆流游泳的小型生物
senses.example: A drifting marine organism cannot choose its water.
senses.exampleCN: 漂浮的海洋生物无法选择自己所在的水。
senses.why: most marine organisms are too small or too weak to swim far, so drifting becomes a defining lifestyle.
senses.whyCN: 多数海洋生物太小或太弱，无法远游，因此漂移成为决定性的生活方式。

senses.title: The bottom-living kind
senses.definition: an organism attached to or crawling on the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 附着于或爬行于海底的生物
senses.example: A bottom-dwelling marine organism may never leave the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 底栖的海洋生物可能一生不离开岩石。
senses.why: the seafloor is a distinct habitat, so the phrase often names organisms defined by that attachment.
senses.whyCN: 海底是一种独立栖息地，因此这个短语常命名由附着方式定义的生物。

senses.title: The swimming kind
senses.definition: an organism strong enough to move against currents
senses.definitionCN: 有足够力量逆流移动的生物
senses.example: A fast marine organism such as a fish can cross the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 像鱼这样快速的海洋生物能横穿海盆。
senses.why: active movement changes how an organism feeds and migrates, so swimming is treated as a separate category.
senses.whyCN: 主动移动改变取食与迁徙方式，因此游泳被视作单独一类。

senses.title: A set of physiological adaptations
senses.titleCN: 生理适应：渗透、压力与温度
senses.definition: the organism considered for how it handles salinity, pressure and cold
senses.definitionCN: 从它如何应对盐度、压力与低温来考虑的生物
senses.example: Every marine organism regulates water and salt across its membranes.
senses.exampleCN: 每种海洋生物都要跨膜调节水与盐。
senses.why: seawater constantly pulls water across membranes, so survival depends on the adaptations the word implies.
senses.whyCN: 海水不断把水拉过膜，因此生存取决于这个词所隐含的适应。

senses.title: A member of a taxonomic group
senses.definition: the organism placed in a group such as bacteria, algae, invertebrates or vertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 被归入细菌、藻类、无脊椎动物或脊椎动物等类群的生物
senses.example: A marine organism may be single-celled or a whale.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物可以是单细胞，也可以是鲸。
senses.why: the phrase cuts across taxonomy, so its content is defined by habitat rather than by relatedness.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语横跨分类系统，因此其内容由栖息地而非亲缘关系决定。

senses.title: An ecological role
senses.titleCN: 生态角色：生产者、消费者、分解者
senses.definition: the organism considered by what it contributes to the food web
senses.definitionCN: 从它对食物网的贡献来考虑的生物
senses.example: A marine organism can be producer, grazer or decomposer.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物可以是生产者、摄食者或分解者。
senses.why: ecology needs roles, not names, so the phrase often stands for a function in a system.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要角色而非名字，因此这个短语常代表系统中的一种功能。

senses.title: A specimen for study
senses.definition: the organism collected, cultured or observed as a specimen
senses.definitionCN: 被采集、培养或观察作为样本的生物
senses.example: The marine organism survived three days in the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 这种海洋生物在水槽中存活了三天。
senses.why: laboratory work turns the category into a countable specimen, which is the sense most experiments use.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作把这个类别变成可计数的样本，这是多数实验使用的义项。

intro.en: Marine organism joins a Latin adjective to a Greek-derived noun. Marine goes back to mare 'sea' through marinus; organism goes back to Greek organon 'tool, organ' plus the noun ending -ismos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine organism 把拉丁形容词接在希腊语源名词上。marine 经 marinus 上溯 mare「海」；organism 上溯希腊 organon「工具、器官」加名词后缀 -ismos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' yielded marinus 'of the sea', which became English marine.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，后者成为英语 marine。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument, organ of the body'; Latin borrowed it as organum.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具、身体器官」；拉丁语借入作 organum。

items.en: The noun organism was formed in English in the eighteenth century from organ plus -ism, meaning an organised living body.
items.cn: 名词 organism 于十八世纪在英语中由 organ 加 -ism 构成，指有组织的活的躯体。

items.en: As biology professionalised, organism became the standard word for any living individual.
items.cn: 随着生物学专业化，organism 成为任何活个体的标准词。

items.en: Oceanography combined the two words to name any sea-dwelling living thing, from bacteria to whales.
items.cn: 海洋学把两个词组合，命名从细菌到鲸的任何海生生物。

items.en: Source uncertain (derivation detail only): the exact sense path from organon 'tool' to organism 'living body' is not fully documented in English sources, though the morphemes are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅派生细节存疑）：从 organon「工具」到 organism「活体」的具体语义路径在英语文献中记载不全，尽管语素本身可靠。

note.en: Group one holds the phrases most often used in place of marine organism; group two holds the general biological words.
note.cn: 第一组是常被用来替代 marine organism 的短语；第二组是泛指生物的词语。

entries.definition: A category of related organisms; one marine organism is an individual of a species.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关生物；一个海洋生物是某一物种的个体。

entries.definition: All sea-dwelling living things taken together; it is a mass term and cannot be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 全部海生生物的集合；是集合名词，不可计数。

entries.definition: The scientific study of marine organisms; it is a field, not a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物的科学；是一个学科，不是生物。

entries.definition: An organism too small to see with the naked eye; it may be marine or not.
entries.definitionCN: 肉眼不可见的生物；可以是海洋的，也可以不是。

entries.definition: Any living individual; it needs a qualifier to say where it lives.
entries.definitionCN: 任何活的个体；需要限定词才能说明生活在哪里。

entries.definition: A general word for a living being, usually an animal; it is informal and rarely used for bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物，通常指动物；较口语，很少用于细菌。

entries.definition: A group capable of interbreeding; it is a category, while an organism is a member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 能相互繁殖的一群生物；它是类别，而个体是该类别的成员。

entries.definition: The drifting organisms of the water column; it is only one subset of marine organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 水柱中漂移的生物；只是海洋生物的一个子集。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin roots, real habitats and real lifestyles, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁词根、真实栖息地与生活方式，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: marine is mare, the sea; organism is a body built of organs: a body in the sea.
normal.cn: marine 是 mare「海」；organism 是由器官构成的躯体：海里的躯体。

normal.en: Three lifestyles divide the group: drifting, bottom-living, swimming.
normal.cn: 三种生活方式划分这一类：漂移、底栖、游泳。

normal.en: Salinity is the constant problem: water wants to leave or enter the body.
normal.cn: 盐度是恒久的问题：水总想离开或进入身体。

normal.en: Pressure rises one atmosphere for every ten metres, which is why deep organisms differ.
normal.cn: 每深十米压力增加一个大气压，因此深水生物与众不同。

normal.en: The phrase crosses taxonomy: a bacterium and a whale are both marine organisms.
normal.cn: 这个短语横跨分类：细菌与鲸都是海洋生物。

abstract.en: A marine organism is a negotiation with salt that never ends.
abstract.cn: 海洋生物是一场与盐永不结束的谈判。

abstract.en: It is a small pocket of fresh chemistry refusing to become seawater.
abstract.cn: 它是一小袋不肯变成海水的化学。

abstract.en: Every sea creature carries its own weather inside a membrane.
abstract.cn: 每个海生生物都在一层膜里带着自己的天气。

examples.en: The survey counted every marine organism larger than a millimetre.
examples.cn: 这次调查统计了所有大于一毫米的海洋生物。

examples.en: A marine organism may be a drifting larva for weeks before settling.
examples.cn: 一种海洋生物可能在漂浮幼体阶段待上数周才定居。

examples.en: The aquarium keeps each marine organism in filtered seawater.
examples.cn: 水族馆把每种海洋生物养在过滤海水中。

dict_mnemonic.text: marine（海的）+ organism（生物体）＝海洋生物；三种生活方式记漂浮、底栖、游泳，核心难题是盐与压力。

root: marine（拉丁 mare「海」→ marinus）+ organism（希腊 organon「工具、器官」+ -ismos）；短语为近代海洋科学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one living thing in salt water: the general category, three lifestyles, its physiology, its taxonomy, its ecological role and its use as a specimen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿咸水中的一个活物展开：总类别、三种生活方式、生理、分类、生态角色，以及作为样本的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body in salt water, constantly trading water and ions across its skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：咸水中的一个小躯体，不断隔着皮肤交换水与离子。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND TAXONOMY: any sea dweller, then its place in a classification.
branches.cn: 类别与分类：先是任何海生者，再是它在分类中的位置。

branches.en: THREE LIFESTYLES: drifting, bottom-living, swimming.
branches.cn: 三种生活方式：漂移、底栖、游泳。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: salt, cold and pressure shape the body.
branches.cn: 生理：盐、低温与压力塑造身体。

branches.en: ROLE: producer, grazer or decomposer in the food web.
branches.cn: 角色：食物网中的生产者、摄食者或分解者。

branches.en: SPECIMEN: the category becomes a countable object of study.
branches.cn: 样本：类别变成可计数的研究对象。

intro.en: Marine organism joins a Latin adjective and a Greek-derived noun, both of which read clearly morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: marine organism 把拉丁形容词与希腊语源名词组合，两者都能按语素清楚读出。

latinIntro.en: Mare provides the Latin entry. Organon is Greek; Latin organum is a borrowing from Greek, not a native cognate, so it is not listed.
latinIntro.cn: mare 提供拉丁条目。organon 属希腊语；拉丁 organum 是从希腊语借入，并非本土同族词，因此不列入。

items.exampleCN: mare 给出 marinus 与 marine。

items.example: Organon is the root of organism.
items.exampleCN: organon 是 organism 的词根。

items.meaning: an organism too small to see
items.exampleCN: 微生物主导着开阔海洋。

items.example: Each marine organism has a salinity strategy.
items.exampleCN: 每种海洋生物都有盐度策略。

items.example: Plankton forms the base of the food web.
items.exampleCN: 浮游生物构成食物网的基础。
游泳生物能横穿整个海盆。

definition_zh: 贸易壁垒；阻碍商品或服务跨境流动的措施
definition_en: a government measure that makes it harder or costlier for goods and services to cross a border
core_image: 公路尽头立着一道横杆，横杆上挂着税率牌与检验章，卡车在横杆前排队等候
scene: 公路尽头立着一道横杆，横杆上挂着税率牌与检验章，卡车排队等候。 A high tariff is the oldest form of trade barrier.
sceneCN: 这里这个词组指「妨碍跨境贸易的措施」（第 1 个义项：阻碍贸易往来的手段）；句意为高关税是最古老的贸易壁垒形式。图中可辨识物件：横杆、税率牌、检验章、排队卡车。

pos.zh: 贸易壁垒（可数；指一项具体措施）

senses.title: Any measure that obstructs cross-border trade
senses.titleCN: 妨碍跨境贸易的任何措施
senses.definition: a government rule whose effect is to slow or block the movement of goods between countries
senses.definitionCN: 其效果在于减慢或阻断货物在国家间流动的政府规定
senses.example: Licensing rules can act as a trade barrier even without a duty.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有关税，许可规则也能起贸易壁垒的作用。
senses.why: The phrase is a picture: trade is a road, and a barrier stands across it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是一幅画：贸易是一条路，一道栏杆横在路前。

senses.title: A tariff on imported goods
senses.titleCN: 对进口货物征收的关税
senses.definition: a tax collected at the border that raises the price of foreign goods
senses.definitionCN: 在边境征收、抬高外国货物价格的税
senses.example: The tariff barrier made imported steel more expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 关税壁垒让进口钢材变得更贵。
senses.why: The oldest barrier is a toll gate, and a tariff is exactly a toll on goods.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的壁垒就是收费门，而关税正是对货物收的门票钱。

senses.title: A quota that limits the quantity
senses.definition: a ceiling on how much of a good may enter in a period
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期内允许进入的货物数量上限
senses.example: The quota barrier kept imports below last year's level.
senses.exampleCN: 配额壁垒把进口量压在上一年水平之下。
senses.why: A gate may open only for a counted number of trucks, which is a barrier of quantity.
senses.whyCN: 一道门可以只放定数的卡车通过，这是数量上的壁垒。

senses.title: A non-tariff barrier of paperwork
senses.titleCN: 由文书手续构成的非关税壁垒
senses.definition: a requirement of forms, inspections or delays that adds cost without adding a tax
senses.definitionCN: 通过表格、检验或拖延增加成本、却不加税的要求
senses.example: Endless paperwork became a non-tariff barrier in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 没完没了的文书实际上成了非关税壁垒。
senses.why: A barrier can be made of time and paper rather than of stone.
senses.whyCN: 壁垒可以由时间与纸张构成，而不必由石头构成。

senses.title: A safety standard used as a barrier
senses.titleCN: 被用作壁垒的安全标准
senses.definition: a technical rule that is reasonable in itself but excludes foreign products in effect
senses.definitionCN: 本身合理、实际上却把外国产品排除在外的技术规则
senses.example: The packaging standard was challenged as a hidden trade barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 这项包装标准被质疑为隐蔽的贸易壁垒。
senses.why: A rule that looks like care can still stand across the road.
senses.whyCN: 一条看起来像出于关照的规则，仍然可以横在路中央。

senses.title: A subsidy that indirectly blocks rivals
senses.titleCN: 间接阻挡竞争者的补贴
senses.definition: support paid to domestic producers that makes foreign goods uncompetitive
senses.definitionCN: 给予本国生产者的支持，使外国货物失去竞争力
senses.example: Farm subsidies can work as a trade barrier without any border tax.
senses.exampleCN: 农业补贴可以在没有任何边境税的情况下充当贸易壁垒。
senses.why: A barrier need not face outward; lifting one side's ground has the same effect.
senses.whyCN: 壁垒不必朝外立；把一边的地基抬高，效果相同。

senses.title: A barrier to entering a market
senses.definition: any cost or rule that keeps a new seller out, including in a domestic market
senses.definitionCN: 把新卖家挡在门外的任何成本或规则，包括在本国市场内
senses.example: The licence is a trade barrier for small importers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项执照对小进口商来说是一道贸易障碍。
senses.why: The road-and-gate image is borrowed for entry in general.
senses.whyCN: 「路与门」的画面被借去指一般的进入。

senses.title: A barrier removed by agreement
senses.definition: a measure that treaties commit countries to lower or abolish
senses.definitionCN: 条约要求各国降低或废除的措施
senses.example: The round of talks removed one trade barrier after another.
senses.exampleCN: 那一轮会谈拆除了一道又一道贸易壁垒。
senses.why: Once barriers are listed in treaties, they become objects that can be taken down.
senses.whyCN: 当壁垒被列进条约，它们就成了可以被拆掉的对象。

intro.en: Trade barrier joins the Germanic word trade with barrier, from Old French barriere, a fence built from bars; the modern policy sense is nineteenth-century.
intro.cn: trade barrier 把日耳曼语的 trade 与 barrier 组合起来；barrier 来自古法语 barriere，指用横杆围成的栅栏；现代政策义出现于十九世纪。

items.en: Barriere named a fence or a gate made of bars, especially one that closed a road into a town.
items.cn: barriere 指用横杆做成的栅栏或门，尤指封住进城道路的那一道。

items.en: The bar itself is usually traced to a spoken Latin word barra, but that form is a reconstruction and its origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 横杆本身常被追溯到口语拉丁语 barra，但该形式属重构，其来源不确定。

items.en: English barrier first meant a physical gate or fence, and then any obstacle that stops movement.
items.cn: 英语 barrier 最初指实体的门或栅栏，后指任何阻挡前进的障碍。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the phrase was applied to duties and rules that stood in the way of commerce between countries.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个短语被用于阻挡国家间商业往来的税与规则。

items.en: After tariffs fell in the twentieth century, the phrase widened to cover standards, licences and paperwork.
items.cn: 二十世纪关税下降之后，这个短语扩展到标准、执照与文书手续。

items.en: Trade rounds turned the barrier into something listed, negotiated and removed clause by clause.
items.cn: 各轮贸易谈判把壁垒变成可以逐条列出、逐条谈掉的东西。

note.en: The first group holds the two parts of the phrase and two look-alikes; the second holds specific measures that count as barriers.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两个组成部分与两个形近词；第二组是算作壁垒的具体措施。

entries.definition: Any fence, gate or obstacle; the longer phrase narrows it to the border of trade.
entries.definitionCN: 任何栅栏、门或障碍；较长的短语把它收窄到贸易边界。

entries.definition: A long piece of metal or wood, and a place that serves drinks; the first is the part a barrier is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 一根长条金属或木头，也指卖酒的店；前者正是构成栅栏的部件。

entries.definition: A lawyer called to the bar; the bar here is a courtroom railing, not a trade gate.
entries.definitionCN: 取得出庭资格的律师；这里的 bar 指法庭围栏，不是贸易关卡。

entries.definition: Buying and selling; it supplies the first half and the thing the barrier obstructs.
entries.definitionCN: 买进卖出；它提供短语前半，也是被阻挡的对象。

entries.definition: A duty on imports; it is one kind of trade barrier, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 对进口征收的税；它是贸易壁垒的一种，而非整个类别。

entries.definition: A fixed maximum of goods allowed in; another single kind of barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 允许进入的货物上限；另一种单一的壁垒。

entries.definition: An official ban on trade with a particular country, the hardest form of barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一国家贸易的官方禁令，是最严厉的壁垒形式。

entries.definition: Any limit placed on an activity; it is broader than trade barrier and may have nothing to do with borders.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项活动施加的任何限制；比贸易壁垒更宽，也可能与边界无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Trade plus barrier: a fence drawn across the road goods must travel.
normal.cn: 「贸易」加「栏杆」：横在货物必经之路上的栅栏。

normal.en: The parts are trade and barrier, the second from a fence of bars.
normal.cn: 组成部分是「贸易」与「栏杆」，后者来自用横杆围成的栅栏。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the kinds: tariff barrier, non-tariff barrier, technical trade barrier.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出种类：关税壁垒、非关税壁垒、技术性贸易壁垒。

normal.en: A tariff is a toll gate; a quota is a counting gate; paperwork is a gate of time.
normal.cn: 关税是收费门，配额是计数门，文书是耗时门。

normal.en: Any listed barrier can be negotiated down, which is why trade rounds exist.
normal.cn: 任何被列出的壁垒都能通过谈判降低，这正是贸易谈判轮次存在的理由。

abstract.en: Picture a road with a gate that charges not money but forms and days.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路，门口的收费不是钱，而是表格与天数。

abstract.en: Picture a wall built one brick at a time, each brick a separate rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵砖墙，每次砌一块，每块砖都是一条单独的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that stands open but has a very high step.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门敞开着，只是门槛非常高。

examples.en: The licensing system operates as a trade barrier in practice.
examples.cn: 这套许可制度实际上起着贸易壁垒的作用。

examples.en: Talks aimed at removing every trade barrier between the two markets.
examples.cn: 会谈旨在拆除两个市场之间的每一道贸易壁垒。

examples.en: A technical standard may be a legitimate safety rule or a hidden trade barrier.
examples.cn: 一项技术标准可能是正当的安全规则，也可能是隐蔽的贸易壁垒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贸易（trade）路上的栏杆（barrier）」——横在跨境买卖前面的关税、配额与手续 → 贸易壁垒

root: trade 来自日耳曼语，本指路径与生活方式，后指买卖；barrier 来自古法语 barriere「横杆围成的栅栏」，其横杆的拉丁语来源属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one fence across a road: any obstructive measure, a tariff gate, a quota gate, a paperwork gate, a safety rule gate, a subsidy that lifts one side, a barrier to entry, and a barrier written into a treaty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道横在路上的栅栏展开：任何阻碍性措施、关税门、配额门、文书门、安全规则门、抬高一边的补贴、进入市场的障碍，以及被写进条约的壁垒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar across a highway with a duty board and an inspection stamp hanging from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在公路上的一道栏杆，上面挂着税率牌与检验章。

branches.en: ANY GATE: a border measure and an entry obstacle are the same bar in two settings.
branches.cn: 任何门：边境措施与进入障碍是同一道栏杆在两种场合。

branches.en: THE TOLL: a tariff is the oldest and most visible form of the bar.
branches.cn: 过路费：关税是最古老、最显眼的栏杆形式。

branches.en: COUNTING AND PAPER: a quota and a form both stop goods by number or by time.
branches.cn: 计数与纸张：配额与表格分别用数量和耗时挡住货物。

branches.en: LOOKS HELPFUL: a safety rule and a subsidy can bar the road from behind the gate.
branches.cn: 看似有益：安全规则与补贴可以从门后把路挡上。

branches.en: REMOVED BY TREATY: once listed, the bar becomes an object negotiators can take down.
branches.cn: 经条约拆除：一旦被列出，栏杆就成了谈判者可以拆掉的对象。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Germanic word for dealing with a French word for a fence, so it reads as a fence standing across commerce.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼语中表示「买卖」的词与法语中表示「栅栏」的词组合起来，读作「横在商业前面的一道栅栏」。

latinIntro.en: Barrier goes back to a spoken Latin word for a bar, recorded only as a reconstruction, so the Latin entries are left empty here.
latinIntro.cn: barrier 可追溯到口语拉丁语中表示「横杆」的词，但该词只有重构形式，因此这里把拉丁语词形一栏留空。

items.structure: Old French barre (a rod, a bar)
items.meaning: a long piece of wood or metal
items.example: The gate is built from iron bars.

items.structure: Old French barriere (a fence of bars)
items.meaning: a fence or gate that stops passage
items.example: A barrier closed the road into the town.
items.exampleCN: 一道栅栏封住了进城的路。

items.example: The duty acted as a trade barrier.
items.exampleCN: 这项税起了贸易壁垒的作用。

items.example: The tariff raised the price at the border.
items.exampleCN: 关税在边境抬高了价格。

items.example: The quota limits the number of crates.
items.exampleCN: 配额限制了木箱的数量。

items.example: A subsidy can make imports uncompetitive.
items.exampleCN: 补贴可以让进口货失去竞争力。

items.meaning: a rule of quality or safety
items.example: A strict standard can exclude foreign goods.
items.exampleCN: 严格的标准可以把外国货物排除在外。

definition_en: very skilled at something; also, a person who is highly skilled
core_image: 老匠人闭着眼也能把活儿做得又快又准
scene: 修理铺里老师傅接了最难的一单，手上的活没有一点犹豫。 The young watchmaker was adept at repairing tiny gears.
sceneCN: 这里 adept 是「熟练的、擅长的」（第 1 个义项：对某事技巧娴熟）；句意为这位年轻钟表匠擅长修理细小齿轮。

pos.zh: 熟练的；擅长的
能手；内行

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「熟练地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「娴熟；精通」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「灵巧；老练」

senses.title: Highly skilled at a craft
senses.definition: very good at doing something that takes skill
senses.definitionCN: 非常擅长需要技巧的事情
senses.example: The young watchmaker was adept at repairing tiny gears.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钟表匠擅长修理细小齿轮。
senses.why: Latin adipisci meant 'to attain'; skill is what one has attained after long practice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adipisci 意为「达到、获得」；技艺正是长久练习后「获得」的东西。

senses.title: A person of high skill
senses.definition: a person who has attained great skill, sometimes with a hint of secret expertise
senses.definitionCN: 技艺高超之人，有时暗指深谙门道者
senses.example: Old practitioners regarded him as an adept of the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 老匠人们视他为这一行的内行。
senses.why: The noun turns attainment into a person: one who has 'arrived' at mastery.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把「已达」变成「已达之人」：抵达精通之境的人。

intro.en: Adept comes from Latin adeptus, 'attained', the participle of adipisci, 'to attain', from ad- plus sequi 'to follow after'.
intro.cn: adept 来自拉丁语 adeptus（已达成的），是 adipisci（达到）的分词，由 ad- 加 sequi（追随）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sek- meant 'to follow'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sek- 意为「跟随」。

items.en: sequi meant 'to follow'; adipisci meant 'to follow after and attain'.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」；adipisci 意为「追随而达成」。

items.en: adeptus meant 'one who has attained'.
items.cn: adeptus 意为「已达成之人」。

items.en: English adept first named alchemists who claimed to have attained the secret.
items.cn: 英语 adept 最初指自称已获炼金秘术的炼金术士。

items.en: Now an ordinary word for skill; the adjective is the commonest form.
items.cn: 如今泛指技艺娴熟；形容词是最常见形式。

note.en: The first group gathers the sequi family; the second gathers words for skill and mastery.
note.cn: 第一组收 sequi 词族；第二组收表示技艺与精通的词。

entries.definition: To adjust to new conditions; only one letter apart, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应、改编」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: To take up and use; look-alike with different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「采纳、收养」；形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The noun for skillfulness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「娴熟」。

entries.definition: Having the training and ability for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有技能的」。

entries.definition: Competent through practice, often with a measure attached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精通的」，常与程度搭配。

entries.definition: Showing the power of a master.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高超的、老练的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the attain root and the adept-at pattern; the abstract hooks picture hands that never hesitate.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「达成」词根与 adept-at 句型；抽象记忆点想象毫不迟疑的手。

normal.en: Adept is adeptus: one who has attained.
normal.cn: adept 出自 adeptus：已达之人。

normal.en: Adept at is the everyday pattern; adept in is formal.
normal.cn: adept at 是日常句型；adept in 偏正式。

normal.en: Watch the triplets adapt, adopt, adept.
normal.cn: 注意三胞胎 adapt、adopt、adept。

normal.en: As a noun, an adept is a master of a craft.
normal.cn: 作名词时，adept 指一门手艺的高手。

normal.en: It once meant an alchemist who found the secret.
normal.cn: 它曾指获得秘术的炼金术士。

abstract.en: Picture hands moving through a task with zero hesitation.
abstract.cn: 想象双手做活时毫无迟疑。

abstract.en: Picture a runner reaching the summit of a skill ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者登上技艺阶梯的顶端。

abstract.en: Picture a closed recipe book finally opened to its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象秘籍终于向主人翻开。

examples.en: The young watchmaker was adept at repairing tiny gears.
examples.cn: 这位年轻钟表匠擅长修理细小齿轮。

examples.en: She is adept at calming angry customers.
examples.cn: 她擅长安抚愤怒的顾客。

examples.en: Old practitioners regarded him as an adept of the trade.
examples.cn: 老匠人们视他为这一行的内行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额代普特」——额头代代普及练出来的本领，就是熟练。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ sequi（跟随）→ adipisci（追而达成）→ adeptus（已达之人）；核心义是「追着技艺跑，直到追上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the skill of the practiced hand, to the person who has attained mastery.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从练熟的手艺，走到已达精通之境的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that never hesitate
core.cn: 核心意象：毫不迟疑的双手

branches.en: Skill shown in smooth, sure performance.
branches.cn: 流畅笃实的表现所显示的技艺。

branches.en: The person who has attained the craft.
branches.cn: 已达精通之境的人。

branches.en: The adjective and noun are one attainment, seen and personified.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词是同一份「达成」的可见态与人化态。

branches.en: Adept at governs the everyday pattern.
branches.cn: adept at 支配日常句型。

branches.en: The alchemist past echoes in this noun sense.
branches.cn: 这个名词义里回响着炼金术士的过去。

intro.en: The word joins ad- with the follow-root seq- through the attainment participle -ept-, and its family keeps sequels and sequences.
intro.cn: 这个词经「达成」分词 -ept- 把 ad- 与「跟随」词根 seq- 结合，词族还保留 sequel 与 sequence。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi and adipisci are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的祖先是拉丁语 sequi 与 adipisci。

definition_zh: 构造地质学；地壳构造运动；建筑构造学
definition_en: the study of the structure and movement of the Earth's crust, or the art of construction
core_image: 一张大地构造图：岩层被压成褶皱、被拉成裂谷，整块地壳像被反复拆装的骨架
scene: 把裂谷两侧的地层对比之后，可以看出这片地形是怎样被塑造的。 The map shows how tectonics has shaped the rift valley over millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里 tectonics 指「构造运动」（第 4 个义项：地壳的构造变形过程）；句意为这张图显示构造运动在数百万年间如何塑造了这条裂谷。

pos.zh: 构造地质学；构造运动；（建筑）构造学

senses.title: The study of crustal structure
senses.titleCN: 构造地质学：研究地壳结构的学科
senses.definition: the branch of geology that studies the structure and deformation of the Earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 研究地壳结构与变形的地质学分支
senses.example: She teaches tectonics at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学讲授构造地质学。
senses.why: A field name ending in -ics treats the subject as a body of knowledge, like physics or economics.
senses.whyCN: 以 -ics 结尾的学科名把研究对象当作一门知识体系，就像 physics 或 economics。

senses.title: Global plate tectonics
senses.definition: the theory and process by which lithospheric plates move and interact
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈板块移动与相互作用的理论和过程
senses.example: Plate tectonics explains both earthquakes and mountain belts.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造学说同时解释了地震与山脉带。
senses.why: The global scale is the modern core of the field: one framework explains many separate phenomena.
senses.whyCN: 全球尺度是这门学科的现代核心：一个框架解释许多彼此分离的现象。

senses.title: Regional structure
senses.definition: the structural history of a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定区域的构造历史
senses.example: The tectonics of the basin record two episodes of rifting.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盆地的构造记录了两期裂谷作用。
senses.why: A region has its own stack of events, so the uncountable field name becomes countable in regional use.
senses.whyCN: 一个区域有自己的一串事件，因此这个不可数的学科名在区域用法中可以具体化。

senses.title: The process of deformation
senses.titleCN: 构造运动：地壳变形的过程
senses.definition: the actual deformation of the crust, such as folding, faulting and rifting
senses.definitionCN: 地壳实际发生的变形，如褶皱、断裂与裂谷作用
senses.example: The map shows how tectonics has shaped the rift valley over millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图显示构造运动在数百万年间如何塑造了这条裂谷。
senses.why: The same noun can name the process rather than the study of the process, just as economics can mean the economy in action.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以指过程而不是对过程的研究，正如 economics 也可指实际运行的经济。

senses.title: The art of construction
senses.definition: in architecture, the discipline of how parts are joined and expressed
senses.definitionCN: 建筑学中研究构件如何拼接与表达的分支
senses.example: His book treats tectonics as the honesty of joints.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书把建筑构造学视为对接缝的诚实表达。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of the root: tekton is a builder, and tectonics is the art of building well.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根最古老的义项：tekton 是建造者，tectonics 就是好好建造的技艺。

senses.title: Structure on other planets
senses.definition: the study of crustal structure and deformation on other rocky bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究其他岩石天体地壳结构与变形的学科
senses.example: Planetary tectonics compares faults on Mars with those on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 行星构造学把火星断层与地球断层作比较。
senses.why: The methods do not depend on the planet, only on whether a body has a brittle shell.
senses.whyCN: 这些方法不取决于哪颗行星，只取决于该天体是否拥有脆性外壳。

senses.title: A style of structural deformation
senses.titleCN: 构造样式：伸展、挤压等类型
senses.definition: a recognised style of deformation, such as extensional or compressional tectonics
senses.definitionCN: 被识别出的变形类型，如伸展构造或挤压构造
senses.example: Extensional tectonics produced a chain of parallel valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 伸展构造形成了一串平行的谷地。
senses.why: Geologists classify deformation by its geometry, so tectonics also names the style rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家按几何形态对变形分类，因此 tectonics 也指某种样式，而不是整个学科。

senses.title: A sequence of structural events
senses.definition: the ordered history of deformation events in a rock body
senses.definitionCN: 一个岩体内变形事件的有序历史
senses.example: The tectonics began with compression and ended with collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的构造演化以挤压开始，以塌陷结束。
senses.why: Structural history is a sequence, so the noun can name the order in which events happened.
senses.whyCN: 构造历史是一个序列，因此这个名词可以指事件发生的先后次序。

intro.en: Tectonics is the noun built on Greek tekton 'builder'. The same word names a science of the Earth and an art of building, two branches of one root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tectonics 是建立在希腊语 tekton「建造者」之上的名词。同一个词既指地球的科学，也指建造的艺术，是同一词根的两条分支。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek tekton 'builder' and tektonike (techne) 'the art of building' supply the root and the notion of a craft.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekton「建造者」与 tektonike (techne)「建造的艺术」提供了词根与「手艺」的概念。

items.en: Latin tectonicus supplied the adjective, and the noun tectonics was formed on the model of other -ics field names.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tectonicus 提供了形容词，名词 tectonics 则按其他 -ics 学科名的模式构成。

items.en: Geologists adopted tectonics for the study of folds, faults and the architecture of the crust.
items.cn: 地质学家采用 tectonics 指对褶皱、断层与地壳架构的研究。

items.en: Architectural writing kept the older craft sense, speaking of the tectonics of a building's joints.
items.cn: 建筑写作保留了更古老的工艺义，用 tectonics 指建筑接缝的构造。

items.en: Plate tectonics became the unifying theory of geology, and the plural-looking form now usually names the global process.
items.cn: 板块构造成为地质学的统一理论，这个看似复数的形式现在通常指全球尺度的过程。

items.en: The deeper history of tekein 'to build' is reconstructed, not attested; a widely cited proposal connects it with a root for weaving or fabricating.
items.cn: tekein「建造」的更早历史是重构而非有记录的；一个被广泛引用的假说把它连到表示编织或制作的词根上。

note.en: Group one separates tectonics from words that look or sound nearly identical; group two separates it from neighbouring Earth-science fields.
note.cn: 第一组把 tectonics 与看起来或听起来几乎相同的词分开；第二组把它与相邻的地球科学领域分开。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'relating to structure'; the noun tectonics names the field or the process.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「与构造有关的」形容词；名词 tectonics 指学科或过程。

entries.definition: the study or practice of a technique. It has the same opening but a different root vowel and a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项技术的研究或实践。开头相同，但词根元音与含义都不同。

entries.definition: a strengthening medicine or a musical keynote. It lacks the tek- opening.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮剂，或音乐的主音。它没有 tek- 开头。

entries.definition: a planned move; the stressed vowel is /æ/, not /e/.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的行动；重读元音是 /æ/ 而不是 /e/。

entries.definition: the whole study of the Earth, including rocks, fossils and history; tectonics is one branch.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的整体学科，包括岩石、化石与历史；tectonics 是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: the process of mountain formation; tectonics covers that and much more, including rifting.
entries.definitionCN: 造山过程；tectonics 覆盖的范围更广，也包括裂谷作用。

entries.definition: the physics of the Earth; it supplies the tools that tectonics uses.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的物理学；它为构造研究提供工具。

entries.definition: an older word for crustal deformation, largely replaced by tectonics.
entries.definitionCN: 指地壳变形的旧术语，现多被 tectonics 取代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots and real neighbouring fields, so the word is anchored in the discipline rather than in a rhyme.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根与真实的相邻学科，因此这个词锚定在学科体系中，而不是靠押韵。

normal.en: tectonics is the noun, tectonic is the adjective, and -ics marks a field like physics or economics.
normal.cn: tectonics 是名词，tectonic 是形容词，-ics 像 physics、economics 一样标记一门学科。

normal.en: tekton means builder, so tectonics studies how the Earth is built and rebuilt.
normal.cn: tekton 表示建造者，所以 tectonics 研究地球如何被搭建与重建。

normal.en: Plate tectonics is the global theory; regional tectonics is its local application.
normal.cn: 板块构造是全球理论；区域构造是它在局部地区的应用。

normal.en: Extensional tectonics pulls the crust apart, compressional tectonics pushes it together.
normal.cn: 伸展构造把地壳拉开，挤压构造把地壳推挤到一起。

normal.en: Architects still use tectonics for the visible logic of joints, which keeps the builder root alive.
normal.cn: 建筑师仍用 tectonics 指接缝的可见逻辑，这使「建造者」词根保持活力。

abstract.en: Abstractly, tectonics is the grammar of assembly: which parts join, in what order, and how the joints show.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tectonics 是组装语法：哪些部件相接、按什么次序、接缝如何显现。

abstract.en: The field and the craft share one idea: a structure is legible when its parts and joins can be read.
abstract.cn: 学科与手艺共享一个观念：当部件与接缝可读时，结构才是清晰的。

abstract.en: Symbol: a folded stack of layers with numbered events along its edge, showing a sequence of deformation.
abstract.cn: 符号：一叠褶皱的岩层，边缘标出编号事件，显示变形的先后序列。

examples.en: Plate tectonics became the central theory of modern geology.
examples.cn: 板块构造成为现代地质学的核心理论。

examples.en: The tectonics of the Andes records long-lived compression.
examples.cn: 安第斯山的构造记录了长期的挤压作用。

examples.en: She wrote a book on the tectonics of stone buildings.
examples.cn: 她写了一本关于石构建筑构造学的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泰克托尼克斯」—— 木匠（tekton）的手艺变成一门学问 → tectonics 构造学

root: 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者）与 tektonike（建造的艺术），加 -ics 构成学科名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tectonics. The thread runs from a field of study to the process it studies, and back to the older craft of building.
sensesIntro.cn: tectonics 的八个义项。主线从一门学科延伸到它所研究的过程，再回到更古老的建造手艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the grammar of how a structure is assembled, whether crust or building.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构如何组装的语法，无论对象是地壳还是建筑。

branches.en: FIELD NAMES: a science of the Earth and a science of other rocky bodies.
branches.cn: 学科名称：关于地球的科学，以及关于其他岩石天体的科学。

branches.en: GLOBAL THEORY: plate tectonics unifies the field.
branches.cn: 全球理论：板块构造把这一领域统一起来。

branches.en: LOCAL HISTORY: a region and a rock body each have an ordered sequence of events.
branches.cn: 局部历史：一个区域和一个岩体都各自有一串有序事件。

branches.en: PROCESS AND STYLE: the noun names both the deformation and its recognised geometry.
branches.cn: 过程与样式：这个名词既指变形本身，也指被识别出的几何样式。

branches.en: CRAFT SENSE: architecture keeps the original art of joining parts.
branches.cn: 手艺义：建筑学保留了拼接构件这门最初的技艺。

intro.en: Tectonics is a root plus a field suffix, and that suffix is productive across the sciences.
intro.cn: tectonics 是一个词根加一个学科后缀，而这个后缀在各科学领域都能产。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek tekton and the noun-forming pattern -ics; scientific Latin passed the adjective tectonicus to English. No separate Latin root family exists here, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分是希腊语 tekton 与构成名词的 -ics 模式；科学拉丁语把形容词 tectonicus 传给英语。这里没有另一支拉丁词根族，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: The root names the maker of the frame.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指骨架的制造者。

items.structure: Greek-derived suffix for fields of study
items.meaning: a discipline or system of knowledge
items.example: Physics and economics use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: physics 与 economics 使用同一个后缀。
这个边缘构造活动活跃。

items.example: Tectonism folded the strata before the intrusion.
items.exampleCN: 在侵入体之前，构造作用已使地层褶皱。

items.meaningCN: 应用于地壳变形的物理学
items.exampleCN: 构造物理学测量应力与应变。

items.meaningCN: 研究与地震有关的构造的学科
items.exampleCN: 地震构造学测绘活动断层。

items.meaning: the theory of moving lithospheric plates
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈板块运动的理论
items.example: Plate tectonics replaced continental drift as the fuller theory.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造作为更完整的理论取代了大陆漂移说。

items.meaningCN: 由拉伸造成的构造变形

definition_zh: 相当程度的；相当大的（用于可分级的性质、感受或状况）
definition_en: a fairly large level of a quality, feeling or condition that can be measured in steps or degrees
core_image: 医生把化验单放在床头，说恢复快慢很大程度取决于病人愿意配合到什么地步
scene: 医生把化验单放在床头，说这位病人恢复得快慢，很大程度取决于他愿意配合到什么地步。 Recovery from the illness requires a considerable degree of patience from the patient.
sceneCN: 这里指耐心这一品质需要的程度相当高（第 1 个义项：不确定或某种性质的程度）；句意为从这场病中恢复需要病人有相当程度的耐心。图中可辨识物件：床头的化验单、医生、病人与家属。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）相当程度的；相当大的

derivatives.zh: 本短语词根对应的动词，义为「考虑、认为」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「考虑、体谅」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在很大程度上」
本短语的核心形容词，义为「相当大的」
本短语的核心名词，义为「程度、度数」
与「程度」一词同出拉丁语「台阶」一词，义为「毕业生；毕业」

senses.title: A high level of a quality
senses.definition: to have a fairly large amount of a quality that can be graded
senses.definitionCN: 指某种可以分级的性质达到相当高的程度
senses.example: The task requires a considerable degree of care if the glass is not to crack.
senses.exampleCN: 若不想让玻璃裂开，这项操作需要相当程度的细心。
senses.why: Degree is a step on a scale, so the phrase measures how many steps up a quality has gone.
senses.whyCN: degree 是刻度上的一级台阶，所以这个短语量的是一种性质往上走了几级。

senses.title: A high level of uncertainty
senses.definition: to contain a fairly large amount of doubt or unpredictability
senses.definitionCN: 指包含相当多的疑问或不可预测的成分
senses.example: The forecast carries a considerable degree of uncertainty beyond five days.
senses.exampleCN: 超过五天的预报带有相当程度的不确定性。
senses.why: Uncertainty is a quality that can be graded, which is why it takes degree rather than amount.
senses.whyCN: 不确定性是一种可以分级的性质，所以它接 degree 而不是 amount。

senses.title: A high level of control
senses.definition: to exercise a fairly large amount of authority or restraint over something
senses.definitionCN: 指对某事物施加相当多的支配或约束
senses.example: The pilot kept a considerable degree of control even in the crosswind.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在侧风里，飞行员仍保持着相当程度的控制。
senses.why: Control can be held partly or fully, so the word pictures a hand on a scale rather than a switch.
senses.whyCN: 控制可以只握住一部分，也可以全握住，所以这个词画的是刻度上的一只手，而不是一个开关。

senses.title: A high level of freedom
senses.definition: to have a fairly large amount of room to act or choose
senses.definitionCN: 指有相当多的行动或选择余地
senses.example: The researchers were given a considerable degree of freedom in choosing their methods.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在选择方法上获得了相当程度的自由。
senses.why: Freedom here is measured, not declared, which is the tone the phrase gives it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的自由是被度量的，而不是被宣告的，这个短语给的正是这种语气。

senses.title: A high level of accuracy
senses.definition: to reach a fairly large amount of precision in measurement or statement
senses.definitionCN: 指在测量或表述上达到相当高的精确度
senses.example: The model can predict the tide with a considerable degree of accuracy near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在近岸能相当精确地预测潮汐。
senses.why: Accuracy comes in steps, and every step up costs something, which is why degrees are counted.
senses.whyCN: 精确是一级一级来的，每上一级都要付出代价，所以要数「度」。

senses.title: A high level of difficulty
senses.definition: to present a fairly large amount of difficulty to someone
senses.definitionCN: 指给某人带来相当多的困难
senses.example: The final section of the exam has a considerable degree of difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 考试的最后一部分有相当大的难度。
senses.why: Difficulty is felt before it is measured, and the phrase puts a number on that feeling.
senses.whyCN: 难度先被感觉到，才被度量，这个短语给那种感觉安上一个数。

senses.title: Degree against extent
senses.titleCN: 程度与范围的用词分工
senses.definition: to measure how much of a quality is present, where extent measures how far something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 指衡量某种性质有多少，而「范围」那一词衡量某事物延伸多远
senses.example: The two plans agree to a considerable degree of similarity, though their extents differ.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个方案在相似程度上相当接近，尽管它们覆盖的范围不同。
senses.why: Degree answers 'how much', extent answers 'how far', and the two frames are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: degree 回答「多少」，extent 回答「多远」，两个框架不能互换。

senses.title: A graded judgement in argument
senses.definition: to make a claim that can be placed on a scale rather than accepted or rejected outright
senses.definitionCN: 指作出的主张可以放在刻度上衡量，而不是只能全盘接受或否定
senses.example: We can accept the proposal to a considerable degree of confidence, but not without a trial.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以在相当高的信心程度上接受这个方案，但仍不能不做试验。
senses.why: The phrase lets an argument admit shades, which is its quiet advantage over yes and no.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让论证容许深浅，这是它相对「是」与「否」的悄悄优势。

intro.en: Consider came from Latin considerare, whose own origin is uncertain: one old proposal connects it with com- and sidus, a star, as observing the heavens, but other accounts exist and none is settled. Degree came through Old French degre from Latin gradus, a step. The quantity phrase is modern and its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: consider 出自拉丁语 considerare，而它本身的来源不确定：一种较早的说法把它与 com- 和 sidus「星」联系起来，指观察星象，但也存在别的解释，没有定论。degree 经古法语 degre 来自拉丁语 gradus「台阶」。量词短语属现代用法，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Considerare meant to examine or weigh carefully, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: considerare 意为仔细察看、权衡，它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: One proposal reads com- plus sidus, star, as a picture of watching the sky for signs; the link is plausible but not established.
items.cn: 一种说法把 com- 与 sidus「星」读作「观天象以判断」的画面；这一联系有道理，但并未确立。

items.en: Gradus meant a step or rank, the rung of a ladder and the unit of a scale.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶或等级，是梯子的一级，也是刻度的一格。

items.en: French degre carried the step image into English as degree.
items.cn: 法语 degre 把「台阶」的画面带进英语，成为 degree。

items.en: Considerable entered English as 'worthy of consideration' before it came to mean 'fairly large'.
items.cn: considerable 进入英语时意为「值得考虑的」，后来才表示「相当大的」。

items.en: A considerable degree of takes a noun, while to a considerable extent is an adverbial phrase, and the two are not interchangeable.
items.cn: 「a considerable degree of」后接名词，而「to a considerable extent」是副词性短语，两者不能互换。

note.en: The first group shares the consider or step root; the second group names neighbouring phrases of level and scale.
note.cn: 第一组共享「权衡」或「台阶」词根；第二组是与「水平、刻度」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: To think about carefully, the verb behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指仔细考虑，是形容词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Careful thought, or a factor to be weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 指仔细思考，或需要考虑的因素。

entries.definition: To a large degree, used with verbs and adjectives.
entries.definitionCN: 指在很大程度上，用于动词与形容词。

entries.definition: A step on a scale, or a unit of temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻度上的一级，或温度单位。

entries.definition: One who has taken the next step in study, from the same step word.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学习上迈出下一步的人，同出「台阶」一词。

entries.definition: A large reach, usually in the frame to a considerable extent.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的范围，常见于表示「在很大程度上」的副词框架。

entries.definition: A large amount of a graded quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指可分级性质的高水平。

entries.definition: A large quantity, used with uncountable nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指大量，接不可数名词。

entries.definition: A big share of a quality, slightly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指某种性质的很大一份，略正式。

entries.definition: The adverbial frame meaning largely.
entries.definitionCN: 指「在很大程度上」的副词框架。

entries.definition: A moderate to large quantity, softer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指中等偏大的量，语气较软。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the uncertain star picture behind consider, the ladder behind degree, and the degree-versus-extent rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「考虑」一词背后不确定的「观星」画面、「程度」一词背后的梯子，以及「程度」与「范围」的分别来记。

normal.en: Consider may come from watching the stars, though the link is uncertain, so treat the picture as a guess.
normal.cn: consider 可能来自观星，但这一联系不确定，所以把画面当作猜测。

normal.en: Gradus is a step, so a degree is one rung on a ladder of more or less.
normal.cn: gradus 是台阶，所以 degree 就是「多与少」这条梯子上的一级。

normal.en: Degree answers how much; extent answers how far, and their frames differ.
normal.cn: degree 回答「多少」，extent 回答「多远」，框架也不同。

normal.en: Use degree of before a noun, and to a considerable extent as an adverb.
normal.cn: 名词前用 degree of，副词性表达用 to a considerable extent。

normal.en: A doctor measuring patience is the picture: a quality placed on a scale.
normal.cn: 医生在量「耐心」，就是画面：一种性质被放上刻度。

abstract.en: Some qualities can only be judged in steps, and the phrase admits that.
abstract.cn: 有些性质只能一级一级地判断，这个短语承认这一点。

abstract.en: A considerable degree is large without being total, which is why it leaves room to argue.
abstract.cn: 相当程度是大而不满，所以它给争论留了余地。

abstract.en: To measure patience is already to have needed some.
abstract.cn: 去量耐心，本身就已经需要一些耐心。

examples.en: The plan carries a considerable degree of uncertainty in its later stages.
examples.cn: 这项计划在后期带有相当程度的不确定性。

examples.en: The two reports show a considerable degree of similarity in their findings.
examples.cn: 这两份报告在结论上显示出相当程度的相似。

examples.en: The work requires a considerable degree of accuracy from the operator.
examples.cn: 这项工作需要操作者相当高的精确度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality on a ladder: care, uncertainty, control, freedom, accuracy, difficulty, the degree-extent split and a graded judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把一种性质放上梯子：细心、不确定、控制、自由、精确、难度、与「范围」一词的分工，以及分级的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor measures how much patience a recovery will demand.
core.cn: 核心意象：医生在衡量一场康复需要多少耐心。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a quality is placed on a ladder and read a few rungs up.
branches.cn: 刻度：一种性质被放上梯子，读出上方好几级。

branches.en: THE DOUBT: uncertainty itself has steps and can be measured.
branches.cn: 疑问：不确定性本身有级差，可以量。

branches.en: THE HAND AND THE ROOM: control can be held partly, and freedom can be granted in measure.
branches.cn: 手与余地：控制可以握住一部分，自由可以按量给予。

branches.en: THE TARGET AND THE WEIGHT: precision is graded, and difficulty is felt before it is counted.
branches.cn: 目标与重量：精确分级，难度先被感觉再被计数。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE ARGUMENT: degree asks how much, extent asks how far, and a claim can be accepted in part.
branches.cn: 框架与论证：degree 问多少，extent 问多远，主张可以被部分接受。

intro.en: The phrase joins an adjective of weighing to a noun of steps, so measurement is built into its two halves.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「权衡」形容词接到「台阶」名词上，两半里都装着度量。

latinIntro.en: Latin considerare supplies the first half; Latin gradus, by way of French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 considerare 提供前半，拉丁语 gradus 经法语提供后半。

definition_zh: n. 入室盗窃者，撬门行窃的人
definition_en: a person who breaks into a building, especially at night, in order to steal

scene: 凌晨三点，门被撬开一条缝，一个人影侧身挤了进来。 A burglar eased the door open at three in the morning.

senses.title: A person who breaks in to steal
senses.definition: someone who enters a building illegally, usually at night, to take things
senses.definitionCN: 非法进入建筑物、常在夜间行窃的人
senses.example: The burglar left the window open behind him.
senses.exampleCN: 窃贼离开时把窗户留在了打开的状态。
senses.why: The word comes from medieval Latin for one who breaks into a fortified place.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自中古拉丁语，指闯入设防之处的人。

senses.title: The alarm named after him
senses.definition: a warning device or system that carries the burglar name
senses.definitionCN: 带有 burglar 之名的报警装置或系统
senses.example: The burglar alarm woke the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 防盗警报吵醒了整条街。
senses.why: English compounds name the device after the thief it is meant to stop.
senses.whyCN: 英语复合词用窃贼之名来称呼用来制止他的装置。

intro.en: Burglar comes from Anglo-French, built on a Latin word for a fortified town.
intro.cn: burglar 源自盎格鲁法语，词根是拉丁语「设防城镇」。

items.en: Burgus means a fortified town.
items.cn: burgus 意为设防城镇。

items.en: Burgator means one who breaks into a house.
items.cn: burgator 意为破门入室者。

items.en: Burgler carries the same meaning.
items.cn: burgler 含义相同。

items.en: English writes burglar for the night thief.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语写作 burglar，指夜间窃贼。

items.en: Burglary becomes a separate legal charge.
items.cn: 十九世纪入室盗窃成为独立罪名。

items.en: Burglar alarm names the warning system.

note.cn: 形近组共享 burg- 词干；近义组按使用暴力的程度排列「窃贼」。

entries.definition: A person who steals.

normalIntro.en: A burglar is the one who breaks the burg, the walled town, and takes what is inside.

normal.en: Burgus meant a walled town.

normal.en: A burgator broke into houses.
normal.cn: burgator 就是破门入室者。

normal.en: English kept the -ar ending.

normal.en: A burglar prefers the dark.
normal.cn: 窃贼偏爱黑暗。

normal.en: A burglary is the crime, to burgle the act.

abstract.en: A door opened without permission.

abstract.en: The quiet hour between lock and alarm.
abstract.cn: 落锁与警报之间的那段安静。

abstract.en: A stranger who knows the house better than you.
abstract.cn: 比你更熟悉这栋房子的陌生人。

examples.en: The burglar took the laptop and nothing else.
examples.cn: 窃贼只拿走了笔记本电脑。

examples.en: The dog next door scared the burglar away.
examples.cn: 隔壁的狗把窃贼吓跑了。
