definition_zh: 炼金术；点石成金的技艺；神奇的转化力
definition_en: a medieval practice of trying to change base metals into gold, or any seemingly magical power of transformation
core_image: 幽暗地窖里的坩埚：铅在火中等待变成黄金的那一刻
scene: 地窖深处，炉火映着满墙的符文手稿。 Medieval alchemy sought to turn lead into gold.
sceneCN: 这里 alchemy 是「炼金术」（第 1 个义项：中世纪试图把贱金属变成黄金的方术）；句意是中世纪炼金术试图将铅变成黄金。

pos.zh: 炼金术；（喻）神奇的转化

collocations.zh: 金融炼金术（虚幻的生财之道）

derivatives.zh: alchemy 加表示人的后缀 -ist，义为「炼金术士」
alchemy 加形容词后缀 -ical，义为「炼金术的；神奇的」
与 alchemy 同源的姊妹词，经阿拉伯语辗转传入，义为「化学」

senses.title: The medieval art of transmutation
senses.definition: the old practice of trying to turn common metals into gold and to find a universal cure
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪试图将贱金属炼成黄金并寻求万灵药的方术
senses.example: Princes kept alchemists hoping that alchemy would refill their treasuries.
senses.exampleCN: 君主们供养炼金术士，指望炼金术能填满国库。
senses.why: The Arabic article al- plus kīmiyā names the craft directly: 'the art of transmutation'.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语定冠词 al- 加 kīmiyā 直接点明这门技艺：「转化之术」。

senses.title: Any seemingly magical transformation
senses.definition: a process that changes something in a mysterious or wonderful way
senses.definitionCN: 以神秘或奇妙的方式改变事物的过程
senses.example: There is a kind of alchemy in the way this kitchen turns leftovers into feasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房能把剩菜变成盛宴，简直有点石成金之妙。
senses.why: If alchemists could raise lead to gold, any astonishing upgrade earns the same name by metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 既然炼金术士能把铅炼成金，任何惊人的升华便可借喻得名。

intro.en: A Greek word for 'poured matter' that travelled through Arabic with its article fused on, then grew into both alchemy and chemistry.
intro.cn: 一个希腊词「浇注之物」，经阿拉伯语时冠词与之熔为一体传入欧洲，后来分出 alchemy 与 chemistry 两个词。

items.en: khēmeia or khumeia meant the art of pouring and mixing, later of transmuting metals; the exact spelling is debated.
items.cn: 希腊语 khēmeia 或 khumeia 意为「浇注混合之术」，后指金属转化术；拼写尚有争议。

items.en: Arabic al-kīmiyāʾ fused the definite article al- onto the borrowed word.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kīmiyāʾ 把定冠词 al- 熔接在借词之上。

items.en: Latin alchemia carried the Arabic form into European scholarship.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 把阿拉伯语形式带入欧洲学术。

items.en: Old French alquemie passed the word to English in the 14th century.
items.cn: 古法语 alquemie 于 14 世纪将该词传给英语。

items.en: The sibling chemistry split off for the science, leaving alchemy to the old art and its metaphor.
items.cn: 其姊妹词 chemistry 分出指称科学，alchemy 留给古方术及其比喻义。

note.en: The first group gathers the word's own offspring and sound-alikes; the second gathers words for mysterious transformation.
note.cn: 第一组收该词的后代词与音近词；第二组收表示「神秘转化」的词。

entries.definition: a person who practises alchemy
entries.definitionCN: 炼金术士

entries.definition: the science of substances, grown out of the same Arabic-Greek word
entries.definitionCN: 化学；与 alchemy 同出一源的姊妹词

entries.definition: an illusion or impossible fantasy; only sounds somewhat similar, unrelated root
entries.definitionCN: 幻想；空想；仅音近，词源无关

entries.definition: relating to alchemy, or magically transformative
entries.definitionCN: 炼金术的；有神奇转化力的

entries.definition: supernatural power, or an enchanting quality
entries.definitionCN: 魔法；魅力

entries.definition: the act of changing one thing into another, the literal goal of alchemy
entries.definitionCN: 嬗变；转化，炼金术的字面目标

entries.definition: the use of magic, often with dark overtones
entries.definitionCN: 巫术；妖术，常带阴暗色彩

entries.definition: magical skill, or extraordinary technical skill
entries.definitionCN: 魔法技艺；（喻）高超本领

entries.definition: a thorough or dramatic change in form or nature
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的改变；变形

normalIntro.en: The al- is the Arabic article 'the', and the rest became chemistry too.
normalIntro.cn: al- 是阿拉伯语定冠词「the」，剩下的部分后来又派生了 chemistry。

normal.en: alchemy and chemistry are twins from one Arabic word.
normal.cn: alchemy 与 chemistry 是同一个阿拉伯词的双生子。

normal.en: alchemist is the person, alchemical the adjective.
normal.cn: alchemist 是人，alchemical 是形容词。

normal.en: Many al- words came from Arabic: alcohol, algebra, alkali.
normal.cn: 许多 al- 开头的词都来自阿拉伯语：alcohol、algebra、alkali。

normal.en: The goal was transmutation: lead into gold.
normal.cn: 其目标是嬗变：点铅成金。

normal.en: Figuratively, alchemy is any wonderful upgrading.
normal.cn: 比喻义上，alchemy 指任何奇妙的升华。

abstract.en: Picture a bubbling crucible glowing orange in a dark cellar.
abstract.cn: 想象幽暗地窖里咕嘟作响、泛着橙光的坩埚。

abstract.en: See grey lead sinking into the pot and a gold coin rising out.
abstract.cn: 想象灰铅沉入锅底，一枚金币浮出水面。

abstract.en: Imagine yesterday's scraps arriving at the table as a banquet.
abstract.cn: 想象昨天的剩料上桌时已成一场盛宴。

examples.en: Isaac Newton devoted years to alchemy.
examples.cn: 牛顿曾花费多年研究炼金术。

examples.en: The novel describes the alchemy of grief into art.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了把悲恸炼成艺术的转化。

examples.en: Critics dismissed the budget as financial alchemy.
examples.cn: 批评者斥这份预算为金融炼金术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱啊渴没」——爱金如渴的术士，最后炼金术没成，化学成了。

root: 希腊语 khēmeia/khumeia「浇注混合之术」借入阿拉伯语为 al-kīmiyāʾ（冠词 al- 熔合），经中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 与古法语 alquemie 于 14 世纪进入英语；同源姊妹词 chemistry 后指科学。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses run from furnace to metaphor: the literal art of making gold, then any wonderful change worth the same name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项从熔炉走向比喻：先是炼金本业，再是一切当得起此名的奇妙转变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crucible in a dark cellar, lead waiting to become gold.
core.cn: 核心意象：幽暗地窖中的坩埚，铅在等待成为黄金。

branches.en: a royal alchemist at a smoking furnace
branches.cn: 在冒着烟的炉前劳作的御用炼金术士

branches.en: manuscripts of symbols and formulas for gold
branches.cn: 写满炼金符号与配方的手稿

branches.en: a kitchen turning scraps into a feast
branches.cn: 把剩料变成盛宴的厨房

branches.en: grief refined into music
branches.cn: 被提炼成音乐的悲恸

branches.en: one promised transformation, in metal or in life
branches.cn: 同一种被许诺的转化，或在金属，或在人生

intro.en: An Arabic definite article welded to a Greek root, with English endings building the family.
intro.cn: 阿拉伯语定冠词焊接在希腊词根上，英语词尾再构筑词族。

latinIntro.en: alchemia is the medieval Latin form through which the word arrived.
latinIntro.cn: alchemia 是该词传入时经由的中世纪拉丁形式。

definition_en: to show or represent something in a picture, a story or words
core_image: 一支笔在纸上落下第一道线，一个侧脸渐渐有了轮廓
scene: 墙上那幅画里，渔民正把网从水里拉起，绳索绷得很紧。 The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
sceneCN: 这里 depict 指用图像表现一个场景（第 1 个义项：用图像描绘）；句意为这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

pos.zh: 描绘；描述；刻画

senses.title: Show in a picture
senses.definition: to represent a scene or person in a painting, drawing or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、素描或照片中表现场景或人物
senses.example: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to paint'; the hand and the pigment are the oldest part of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「绘画」；手与颜料是这个词最古老的部分。

senses.title: Describe in words
senses.definition: to describe something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或文字描述某事物
senses.example: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。
senses.why: Words paint too: the same verb serves the brush and the pen because both make a scene visible.
senses.whyCN: 文字也在作画：同一个动词服务画笔与钢笔，因为两者都让场景变得可见。

senses.title: Portray a character
senses.definition: to present a person in a story with particular traits
senses.definitionCN: 在故事中呈现具有特定特征的人物
senses.example: The author depicts her as generous but proud.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她刻画得慷慨却骄傲。
senses.why: A character is built line by line, and the word covers the accumulation of those lines.
senses.whyCN: 人物是一笔一笔建起来的，这个词涵盖的就是这些笔画的累积。

senses.title: Represent symbolically
senses.definition: to stand for something larger through an image
senses.definitionCN: 通过图像代表更宏大的事物
senses.example: The mural depicts peace as a white bird over ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 壁画把和平表现为废墟上的一只白鸟。
senses.why: A symbol is a picture that carries more than it shows, and depiction is how that load is attached.
senses.whyCN: 象征是一幅承载多于其所显示之物的画，而描绘就是附上这份重量的方式。

senses.title: Present a scene vividly
senses.definition: to set a scene before the reader's or viewer's mind
senses.definitionCN: 把场景呈现在读者或观者心中
senses.example: The opening chapter depicts a storm at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇一章呈现了海上风暴。
senses.why: Vividness depends on selection: a few details make the whole scene appear.
senses.whyCN: 生动取决于取舍：少数细节就能让整个场景浮现。

senses.title: Reflect accurately
senses.definition: to show something as it really is, without distortion
senses.definitionCN: 不失真地显示事物的真实样貌
senses.example: The report depicts conditions in the camp honestly.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告如实反映了营地里的状况。
senses.why: When accuracy is the goal, depiction becomes a test of honesty rather than skill.
senses.whyCN: 当目标是准确时，描绘就成了对诚实的检验，而不只是对技巧的检验。

senses.title: Portray in a certain light
senses.definition: to present someone or something with a chosen bias
senses.definitionCN: 带着选定的偏向呈现某人或某物
senses.example: The article depicts the reform as a disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把改革描绘成一场灾难。
senses.why: Every depiction chooses an angle, and the choice can be innocent or deliberate.
senses.whyCN: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，而这个选择可以无辜，也可以是有意。

senses.title: Graphic representation
senses.definition: to represent data or structure by a diagram
senses.definitionCN: 用图表表现数据或结构
senses.example: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。
senses.why: A diagram is depiction stripped to relations: no faces, only lines that show what connects to what.
senses.whyCN: 图表是被剥到只剩关系的描绘：没有面孔，只有显示连接关系的线。

intro.en: Depict comes from a Latin verb meaning to paint, and painting remains its core image.
intro.cn: depict 来自一个意为「绘画」的拉丁动词，绘画始终是它的核心意象。

items.en: English borrowed depict in the 17c. for painting and later extended it to writing and diagrams.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 depict，指绘画，后来扩展到文字与图表。

items.en: Depingere meant 'to paint, portray', built from de- and pingere 'to paint'.
items.cn: depingere 意为「绘画、描绘」，由 de- 与 pingere「画」构成。

items.en: Pingere 'to paint' also gives picture and pigment, both about colour laid on a surface.
items.cn: pingere「画」也产生 picture 与 pigment，两者都关于涂在表面上的颜色。

items.en: Pictura meant 'painting' and supplied English pictura and pictorial through other routes.
items.cn: pictura 意为「绘画」，并通过其他路径提供英语的 pictorial 等词。

items.en: The verb widened from canvas to language, so that a sentence can depict a scene no one has painted.
items.cn: 这个动词从画布扩展到语言，于是一句话也可以描绘无人画过的场景。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pict stem; the near-meaning group names ways of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 pict 词干；近义组列出各种呈现方式。

entries.definition: a picture or description of something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的图画或描述。

entries.definition: shown in a picture or words.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中显示的。

entries.definition: serving to represent something.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表现某物的。

entries.definition: expressed in pictures rather than words.
entries.definitionCN: 以图画而非文字表达的。

entries.definition: to show a person or thing in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 以特定方式表现人或物。

entries.definition: to give a spoken or written account of something.
entries.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式叙述某物。

entries.definition: to make something clear by examples or pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 用例子或图画使某物清楚。

entries.definition: to represent something in a particular medium or style.
entries.definitionCN: 以特定媒介或风格表现某物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a hand making the first line of a face.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「一只手画出一张脸的第一道线」的画面留住。

normal.en: Depict shares a root with picture: both come from the Latin verb to paint.
normal.cn: depict 与 picture 同根：两者都来自拉丁语「画」的动词。

normal.en: Picture a painter blocking in a face with three strokes.
normal.cn: 想象画家用三笔勾出一张脸的轮廓。

normal.en: A diagram is a depiction with no faces, only connections.
normal.cn: 图表是没有面孔的描绘，只有连接。

normal.en: Say dih-PIKT, like a brush tapping the canvas.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-PIKT，像画笔点在画布上。

normal.en: Link it with describe: one paints for the eye, the other for the ear.
normal.cn: 把它和 describe 联系：一个为眼睛作画，一个为耳朵叙述。

abstract.en: Every depiction chooses an angle and leaves something out.
abstract.cn: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，并遗漏了某些东西。

abstract.en: Words can paint a scene no one has ever seen.
abstract.cn: 文字可以画出无人见过的场景。

abstract.en: Accuracy in depiction is a form of honesty.
abstract.cn: 描绘中的准确，是一种诚实。

examples.en: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
examples.cn: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

examples.en: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
examples.cn: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。

examples.en: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
examples.cn: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（向下）+ pict（画）：把形象画下来，就是「描绘」。

root: 拉丁语 depingere（绘画）：de- + pingere（画）

sensesIntro.en: Depict always makes something visible, whether to the eye or to the mind; the senses differ in the medium and in the honesty of the showing.
sensesIntro.cn: depict 始终让某物变得可见，无论对眼睛还是对心智；各义项的差别在于媒介，以及这种显示是否诚实。

branches.en: Pictures and vivid scenes made for the eye.
branches.cn: 为眼睛而作的图画与生动场景。

branches.en: Words that build a scene or a person.
branches.cn: 构建场景或人物的文字。

branches.en: Images that carry a meaning larger than themselves.
branches.cn: 承载着大于自身的意义的图像。

branches.en: Honest or slanted versions of the same thing.
branches.cn: 同一事物诚实或有偏向的版本。

branches.en: Diagrams that show only relations.
branches.cn: 只显示关系的图表。

intro.en: The word's family is built on the Latin verb for painting.
intro.cn: 这个词的词族建立在拉丁语「绘画」动词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere and pictura supply several English words about images and colour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pingere 与 pictura 提供了若干关于图像与颜色的英语词。

items.meaning: the act or result of showing
items.example: The film's depiction of war is restrained.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影对战争的表现很克制。

items.meaning: shown in an image or account
items.meaningCN: 在图像或叙述中显示的
items.example: The scene is depicted in three panels.

items.example: A fresco depicting the harvest covers the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一幅描绘收获的壁画覆盖整面墙。
摄影是一种再现性的媒介。

items.exampleCN: 这位描绘宫廷生活的人是个小画家。

items.example: The magazine is famous for its pictorial coverage.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志以图片报道闻名。

items.example: The village is almost too picturesque.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄几乎美得像画。
有些悲伤几乎无法表现。

definition_en: a sequence of steps in which a liquid or gas is passed through a barrier that holds back solid particles
core_image: 水从进水口流进砂层，穿过一层层砂砾，从底部滴出清水
scene: 水厂的砂滤池里，浑水从上方流入，穿过厚厚的砂层，从池底流出时已经变清。 The filtration process removes particles at every metre of sand.
sceneCN: 这里 filtration process 指把固体从液体中分离的整套操作步骤（第 1 个义项：过滤工艺流程）；句意为这套过滤流程在每一米砂层里都在去除颗粒。图中可辨识物件：砂滤池、进水口、砂层、出水口。

pos.zh: 过滤流程；过滤工序（可数）
（信息或人员的）筛选流程

senses.title: A sequence that separates solids from fluid
senses.titleCN: 把固体从流体中分离的流程
senses.definition: the ordered series of steps by which a liquid or gas is passed through a barrier so that solid particles are held back
senses.definitionCN: 让液体或气体通过屏障、使固体颗粒被截留的有序步骤
senses.example: The filtration process begins when the slurry enters the drum.
senses.exampleCN: 当浆料进入转鼓，过滤流程就开始了。
senses.why: the phrase joins a process noun to a barrier noun, so it names not one action but the whole route from feed to clear output.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「过程」与「屏障」并置，命名的不是单个动作，而是从进料到清水输出的整条路线。

senses.title: The treatment stage at a waterworks
senses.definition: the stage in municipal water treatment in which water percolates through sand or another medium to remove suspended particles
senses.definitionCN: 市政水处理中让水渗过砂层或其他介质以去除悬浮物的阶段
senses.example: The filtration process removes particles down to five micrometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这套过滤工序能去除小到五微米的颗粒。
senses.why: a stage in a larger works is itself a process, so the phrase marks both its internal steps and its place in the plant.
senses.whyCN: 大厂中的一道工序本身也是流程，因此这个短语既指其内部步骤，也指它在厂中的位置。

senses.title: A laboratory procedure
senses.definition: the standard laboratory procedure of pouring a mixture through filter paper and collecting the clear liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把混合物经滤纸倒过、收集清液的实验室标准步骤
senses.example: The filtration process left a clear filtrate in the flask.
senses.exampleCN: 过滤步骤在烧瓶里留下了清澈的滤液。
senses.why: the same few moves, poured, waited, collected, become a repeatable procedure with a fixed order.
senses.whyCN: 倒、等、收这几个相同动作构成一个顺序固定的可重复步骤。

senses.title: A continuous industrial run
senses.definition: an industrial process in which feed and filtrate flow without stopping, as on a rotary drum or a belt
senses.definitionCN: 进料与滤液不停流动的工业流程，如转鼓或带式过滤
senses.example: A continuous filtration process runs without stopping the feed.
senses.exampleCN: 连续过滤流程不必停止进料即可运行。
senses.why: making the steps continuous turns a batch operation into a flow, and the phrase keeps the word process for that flow.
senses.whyCN: 把步骤连起来就把分批操作变成流动，短语仍用 process 指这股流程。

senses.title: The kidney's filtering sequence
senses.definition: the physiological sequence in which blood plasma is forced through a membrane in the kidney while cells and large proteins are retained
senses.definitionCN: 血浆在肾脏被压过膜、细胞与大分子蛋白被留下的生理顺序
senses.example: The kidney's filtration process handles about a hundred and eighty litres a day.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏的滤过过程每天处理约一百八十升。
senses.why: physiology describes an organ as a plant with stages, so the industrial phrase fits the body without strain.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把一个器官描述成有工序的工厂，因此工业短语用在身体上毫无违和。

senses.title: A review that removes unreliable items
senses.titleCN: 筛除不可靠内容的流程
senses.definition: a staged review by which information, claims or applications are checked and those that fail are removed
senses.definitionCN: 分阶段审查信息、主张或申请，并移除不合格者的流程
senses.example: The agency described its review as a filtration process for unreliable claims.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把审查描述为筛除不可靠说法的流程。
senses.why: once filtering is a process rather than a single pass, review boards can borrow the phrase for their own stages.
senses.whyCN: 一旦过滤被视为多阶段流程而非一次通过，审查机构就能借这个短语描述自己的阶段。

senses.title: Several barriers in series
senses.definition: a process that passes the same fluid through two or more barriers, each catching finer particles than the last
senses.definitionCN: 让同一流体依次通过两道或多道屏障，每道截住比上一道更细的颗粒
senses.example: The plant uses a two-stage filtration process.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂采用两级过滤流程。
senses.why: stages in series are the clearest proof that filtration is a process: each output becomes the next input.
senses.whyCN: 串联的级数最能证明过滤是一个流程：每一级的输出成为下一级的输入。

senses.title: A mechanism that sorts people or ideas
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：逐层筛选的机制
senses.definition: used figuratively of an institutional mechanism that removes unusual or unwanted candidates at each stage
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指在每一阶段剔除不寻常或不合需要的候选者的制度机制
senses.example: Hiring became a filtration process that removed unusual candidates.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘变成一道过滤流程，把不寻常的候选者筛掉了。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the staged structure and replaces particles with people, which shows how strongly the process image shapes institutions.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留分级结构，把颗粒换成人，可见「流程」意象对制度的影响之深。

intro.en: The phrase joins filtration, from Medieval Latin filtrum 'felt', to process, from Latin processus 'a going forward', the participle of procedere 'to go forward'. Both parts are old; the compound is modern technical English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把出自中世纪拉丁 filtrum「毛毡」的 filtration 与出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」的 process 组合起来，后者是 procedere「向前走」的分词。两部分都古老，组合本身是现代技术英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Filtrum meant 'felt' and then 'a felt strainer'; the material gave its name to the barrier and, through filtration, to the whole operation.
items.cn: filtrum 先指「毛毡」，再指「毡制滤器」；材料把名字给了屏障，又经 filtration 给了整个操作。

items.en: Procedere 'to go forward' joins pro- 'forward' to cedere 'to go', and its participle processus named a advance or a course of events.
items.cn: procedere「向前走」由 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」构成，其分词 processus 命名一次前进或一串事件。

items.en: English process, recorded from the fourteenth century, first meant a course or progression and later a series of operations in manufacture.
items.cn: 英语 process 自十四世纪有记录，初指进程或经过，后指制造中的一系列操作。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century engineering put the two nouns together to name the whole route rather than a single step.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的工程把这两个名词并置，命名整条路线而非单个步骤。

items.en: Water treatment, chemical engineering and medicine each adopted the phrase for their own staged separations, and administration borrowed it for reviewing people.
items.cn: 水处理、化学工程与医学各自采用这个短语描述自己的分级分离，行政则借它描述对人的审查。

items.en: Source uncertain (combination date): no single citation fixes when the two words were first used together, and the Germanic form behind filtrum is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（组合年代）：没有单一书证能确定这两个词最早何时连用，且 filtrum 背后的日耳曼形式属于重构。

note.en: Group one holds the parts of the phrase and its near relatives; group two holds other named treatment processes that do a similar job.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的组成部分及其近亲；第二组是做类似工作的其他处理流程名称。

entries.definition: The separation itself; the full phrase adds the idea of ordered stages.
entries.definitionCN: 分离本身；完整短语加入了有序阶段的意思。

entries.definition: The barrier that performs the separation, not the sequence around it.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分离的屏障，而非围绕它的顺序。

entries.definition: Any course of operations; it needs filtration to say which operation is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 任何一串操作；需要 filtration 来指明是哪一种操作。

entries.definition: Recorded events or legal steps, from the same verb; they are a course of events, not a manufacturing route.
entries.definitionCN: 被记录的事件或法律步骤，出自同一动词；是一串事件，不是制造路线。

entries.definition: Any splitting of a mixture; a filtration process is one way to reach it.
entries.definitionCN: 把混合物分开的任何做法；过滤流程是达到它的一种方式。

entries.definition: Making something pure; a filtration process may be one stage of purification.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物纯净；过滤流程可能是提纯的一个阶段。

entries.definition: Checking people or data against a standard; close to the figurative sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 按标准检查人或数据；接近该短语的比喻义。

entries.definition: A whole set of operations applied to water or waste; filtration is normally one stage inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 施加于水或废物的一整套操作；过滤通常是其中一级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Filtrum 'felt' plus processus 'a going forward': a barrier plus a route.
normal.cn: filtrum「毛毡」加 processus「向前行进」：一道屏障加一条路线。

normal.en: The phrase names the whole route, while filtration alone names the separation.
normal.cn: 这个短语命名整条路线，单说 filtration 则只命名分离本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: two-stage, continuous, water filtration process.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：两级、连续、水过滤流程。

normal.en: Physiology says glomerular filtration process, the kidney's own production line.
normal.cn: 生理学说肾小球滤过过程，即肾脏自己的生产线。

normal.en: The institutional phrase is a filtration process for applications, where people are the particles.
normal.cn: 制度说法是申请的筛选流程，那里人就是被截住的颗粒。

abstract.en: Picture water entering at the top of a sand tank and leaving clear at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象水从砂池顶部进入，从底部清亮地流出。

abstract.en: Picture a queue passing three desks, each sending some people home.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人经过三张桌子，每张都让一些人回家。

abstract.en: Picture one sieve above another, each catching finer grains.
abstract.cn: 想象一个筛子叠在另一个筛子上，各自截住更细的颗粒。

examples.en: The filtration process at the plant is checked every morning before the first sample is taken.
examples.cn: 工厂每天早晨在取样前检查过滤流程。

examples.en: Engineers shortened the filtration process by adding a second drum.
examples.cn: 工程师增加了一个转鼓，缩短了过滤流程。

examples.en: The committee turned the grant review into a filtration process with three stages.
examples.cn: 委员会把资助评审变成一道分三阶段的筛选流程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「过滤 + 流程」——从进料到清水的一整套步骤：过滤流程

root: filtration（中世纪拉丁 filtrum「毛毡、滤器」）+ process（拉丁 processus「向前行进」，出自 procedere = pro-「向前」+ cedere「走」）。两词并置构成现代技术短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one route: slurry enters a drum, water seeps through a sand bed, a laboratory pours through paper, a plant runs continuously, a kidney filters blood, a board screens claims, barriers stand in series, and finally an institution filters candidates.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一条路线：浆料进入转鼓，水渗过砂床，实验室用滤纸倒过，工厂连续运行，肾脏过滤血液，委员会筛除说法，多道屏障串联，最后是机构筛选候选者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: muddy water entering the top of a sand tank and leaving clear at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：浑水从砂池顶部进入，从底部清亮地流出。

branches.en: THE ROUTE AT THREE SCALES: a drum, a sand bed and a filter paper all run the same short sequence.
branches.cn: 三个尺度的同一路线：转鼓、砂床与滤纸都在跑同一段短流程。

branches.en: CONTINUOUS FLOW: feeding and drawing off without stopping turns steps into a stream.
branches.cn: 连续流动：不停进料与出料，把步骤变成一股水流。

branches.en: THE BODY'S PRODUCTION LINE: a kidney runs the industrial route inside a living body.
branches.cn: 体内的生产线：肾脏在活体内跑着工业路线。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATIVE FILTERING: claims and candidates are passed through stages until only acceptable ones remain.
branches.cn: 行政筛选：说法与候选者被送过各阶段，直到只剩可接受者。

branches.en: SERIES OF BARRIERS: each stage takes the output of the last, which is what makes the sequence a process.
branches.cn: 串联屏障：每一级接过上一级的输出，这才让整串步骤成为流程。

intro.en: The phrase combines a noun of felt with a noun of going forward, and each half brings its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「毛毡」名词与「向前行进」名词组合起来，两半各自带来一族词。

latinIntro.en: Filtrum gives filter and filtration; procedere gives process, proceed, procedure and proceedings.
latinIntro.cn: filtrum 衍生 filter 与 filtration；procedere 衍生 process、proceed、procedure 与 proceedings。

items.example: The first half of the phrase comes from this noun.
items.exampleCN: 短语的前一半出自这个名词。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of the course.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出进程的方向。

items.example: The verb begins the process family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词开启 process 词族。
这个名词成为英语 process。

items.meaning: a fixed way of doing something
items.example: The procedure is written on the wall.

definition_zh: 分母；分数线下方的数；除数；比率中的后项；共同特征
definition_en: the number below the line in a fraction, which names the size of the parts, or a shared basis for comparison
core_image: 分数横线下方的数字被蓝笔圈出，像给每一份贴上规格标签
scene: 分数横线下方的数字被蓝笔圈出，旁边画着一块被平分的小方块。 The denominator names the size of each part in the fraction.
sceneCN: 这里 denominator 指「分数中写在横线下方的数，说明每份的大小」（第 1 个义项：分数的分母）；句意为分母给这个分数里每一份的大小命名。图中可辨识物件：分数横线、蓝笔圈、被平分的小方块、上下两个数字。

pos.zh: 分母；除数；比的后项；共同点

derivatives.zh: 分母的；与分母有关的（数学用法）
命名；给……定名（同出拉丁 denominare）
名称；教派；面额（同出拉丁 denominare）
名义上的；标称的（同出拉丁 nomen）
用词不当；错误名称（同出拉丁 nomen）

senses.title: The number below the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that names the size of each equal part
senses.definitionCN: 分数中给每个等份的大小命名的那个数
senses.example: The denominator names the size of each part in the fraction.
senses.exampleCN: 分母给这个分数里每一份的大小命名。
senses.why: denominator is Latin for 'namer': the bottom number names what kind of part is being counted, thirds or fifths.
senses.whyCN: denominator 在拉丁语里是「命名者」：下面那个数命名被数的是几分之几。

senses.title: The divisor in a division
senses.definition: the quantity by which another quantity is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来去除另一个量的那个量
senses.example: In the long division, the denominator stands outside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，除数写在除号外面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the bottom number plays exactly the role of the divisor.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此下面那个数扮演的正是除数的角色。

senses.title: The second term of a ratio
senses.definition: the second quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时后说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the denominator is the whole to which the part is compared.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，后项是被拿去比较的那一整个。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction put into words, so the second term takes the seat of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此后项坐的就是下面那个数的位置。

senses.title: A common denominator as a shared basis
senses.titleCN: 引申义：共同点、共同基础
senses.definition: a feature shared by different things that makes them comparable
senses.definitionCN: 不同事物共有、使它们可以相互比较的特征
senses.example: A love of cheap travel was the common denominator of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 喜欢便宜的旅行是这个群体的共同点。
senses.why: fractions can only be added when they share a denominator, so the shared bottom number became a metaphor for shared ground.
senses.whyCN: 分数只有在分母相同时才能相加，于是共同的下面那个数成了「共同基础」的比喻。

senses.title: The least common denominator
senses.definition: the smallest number that can serve as the denominator of two or more fractions
senses.definitionCN: 能同时作为两个或更多分数分母的最小那个数
senses.example: Finding the least common denominator made the addition simple.
senses.exampleCN: 找到最小公分母让加法变简单了。
senses.why: the smallest shared bottom number is the practical choice when fractions must be combined, so it has its own fixed name.
senses.whyCN: 分数必须合并时，最小的共同下面那个数就是实用选择，因此它有自己的固定名称。

senses.title: The population at risk in a rate
senses.definition: the total number of people or items over which an event count is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来除事件计数的那个总人数或总物件数
senses.example: The denominator of the death rate is the whole population at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 死亡率的分母是处在风险中的全部人口。
senses.why: a rate is events over population, and the population below the line is literally the denominator.
senses.whyCN: 率就是事件数除以人口数，写在横线下方的人口就是字面意义上的分母。

senses.title: The denominator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分母多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written below the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线下方的那个多项式
senses.example: A zero of the denominator polynomial leaves the expression without a value.
senses.exampleCN: 分母多项式的零点会让表达式没有可取的值。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions, so the bottom polynomial keeps the name of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式照搬普通分数，因此下面那个多项式沿用下面那个数的名字。

senses.title: Rationalizing the denominator
senses.definition: the operation of removing a root or irrational number from the bottom of a fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把根号或无理数从分数下方去掉的运算
senses.example: Rationalizing the denominator made the exact value easier to read.
senses.exampleCN: 有理化分母后，精确值更容易读出来。
senses.why: the operation is named after the part it cleans, the denominator at the bottom of the fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算以它清理的那一部分命名，也就是分数下方的分母。

senses.title: An older word for a namer
senses.definition: an older use for a person or thing that gives a name
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物定名的人或物
senses.example: In the old text, the denominator of each district was the clerk who named it.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧文献里，每个辖区的命名者就是给它定名的书记。
senses.why: Latin denominare meant 'to name', and the agent noun kept that literal sense long before fractions adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 denominare 意为「命名」，这个施动名词在分数借用它之前很久就保留着这个字面义。

intro.en: Denominator comes from Latin denominare 'to name', built on de- plus nomen 'name'. The fraction sense arrives through French dénominateur, because the bottom number names the kind of part.
intro.cn: denominator 来自拉丁 denominare「命名」，由 de- 加 nomen「名字」构成。分数义经法语 dénominateur 而来，因为下面那个数为「哪一种份」命名。

items.en: Nomen meant 'name'. It is the source of nominal, nomination, misnomer and the nomen in denominator.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」。它是 nominal、nomination、misnomer 的来源，也是 denominator 里的那个 nomen。

items.en: Nominare meant 'to name, call', a verb formed on nomen; its compounds name things in many directions.
items.cn: nominare 意为「命名、称呼」，由 nomen 构成的动词；它的复合形式向多个方向给事物命名。

items.en: De- plus nominare gave denominare 'to name, designate', with the prefix adding completion or specification.
items.cn: de- 加 nominare 构成 denominare「命名、指称」，前缀增添「彻底、具体化」的意思。

items.en: French formed dénominateur for the bottom number of a fraction, since that number names what size the parts are.
items.cn: 法语构成 dénominateur，指分数下面那个数，因为这个数命名每份的大小。

items.en: English adopted denominator in the sixteenth century, and the figurative 'common denominator' followed as fractions became everyday knowledge.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪接受了 denominator，随着分数成为常识，比喻义的「共同点」也随后出现。

items.en: The exact first citation for the figurative sense is approximate; nomen and nominare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 比喻义的最早确切书证为约数；nomen 与 nominare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for name and is easy to confuse; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「名字」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give a name or express in a unit; it is an action, not the bottom number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为命名或以某单位表示；是动作，不是下面那个数。

entries.definition: A name, a religious body, or a unit value of money; it never means the bottom of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指名称、教派或货币面额；从不指分数的下方。

entries.definition: In name only, or stated rather than real; it keeps nomen without the de- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指名义上的或标称的；保留 nomen 但没有那个表示「离开」的前缀。

entries.definition: A wrong or unsuitable name; it is built on nomen and names a naming error, not a fraction part.
entries.definitionCN: 指错误或不恰当的名称；由 nomen 构成，命名的是命名错误，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The top number, built on numerus 'number'; it counts parts while the denominator names them.
entries.definitionCN: 上面那个数，建立在 numerus「数」上；它负责数份数，而分母负责命名。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; in a fraction it is the number below the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来除的那个数；在分数里就是横线下方的数。

entries.definition: The second term of a ratio, matching the denominator's position.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的后项，对应分母的位置。

entries.definition: A foundation or starting value; a common denominator is a figurative base for comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 指基础或起始值；公分母是用于比较的比喻性基础。

entries.definition: A standard used to judge; a common denominator is a shared feature, not a rule of judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于判断的标准；公分母是共有特征，不是判断规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根与后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: nomen 'name' plus de- plus -ator: the namer at the bottom tells you what kind of part it is.
normal.cn: nomen「名字」加 de- 与 -ator：下面那个命名者告诉你这是几分之几。

normal.en: The family runs denominator, denominate, denomination, nominal and misnomer, all from nomen.
normal.cn: 同族词有 denominator、denominate、denomination、nominal 与 misnomer，都出自 nomen。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: common denominator, least common denominator, rationalize the denominator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：公分母、最小公分母、有理化分母。

normal.en: The denominator names; the numerator counts. Name below, count above.
normal.cn: 分母负责命名，分子负责数数：名字在下，数在上。

normal.en: Two fractions can only be added when their denominators agree, which is why shared ground is called common.
normal.cn: 两个分数只有分母一致才能相加，这就是「共同基础」被称作「公」的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting a cake into equal slices and writing the slice size on each one.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀把蛋糕切成等份，并在每一片上写出这一份的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of strangers who all discover they speak the same language.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子陌生人忽然发现彼此说同一种语言。

abstract.en: Picture a group of people counted against the whole town, with the town written below the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被拿去与整个镇子相比，镇子的数目写在横线下方。

examples.en: A fraction with zero as its denominator is not defined.
examples.cn: 分母为零的分数没有定义。

examples.en: The two groups were compared on a common denominator of income.
examples.cn: 这两个群体按收入的共同基础来比较。

examples.en: Rationalizing the denominator removed the root from the bottom.
examples.cn: 有理化分母把根号从下方去掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得名」——下面那个数给整块「定名」，说明是几分之几 → 分母

root: 拉丁 nomen「名字」→ nominare「命名」→ denominare「定名」→ 法语 dénominateur（分数下方的命名者）→ 英语 denominator。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one role: the number or feature that names the size of the parts. It names parts of a fraction, the divisor, the second term of a ratio, a shared basis, a population base, a polynomial and a cleaned root.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都保留同一个角色：为「每一份有多大」命名的那一个数或特征。它命名分数的份、除数、比的后项、共同基础、人口基数、多项式，以及被清理掉的根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number below the fraction bar, circled in blue like a label on each slice.
core.cn: 核心意象：分数横线下方的数，被蓝笔圈住，像每一份上的规格标签。

branches.en: THE NAMING NUMBER: the bottom number tells you the size of each part.
branches.cn: 命名的数：下面那个数告诉你每一份有多大。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the divisor of a division and the second term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的除数与比的后项。

branches.en: SHARED GROUND: a common bottom number, and the smallest one that two fractions can share.
branches.cn: 共同基础：共同的下面数，以及两个分数能共用的最小那个。

branches.en: WHAT THE LINE DIVIDES BY: the population at risk in a rate, and the polynomial below an algebraic fraction.
branches.cn: 横线用来除什么：比率中的风险人口，以及代数分式下方那个多项式。

branches.en: CLEANING AND NAMING: rationalizing removes a root from the bottom, while the oldest sense is a person who names.
branches.cn: 清理与命名：有理化把根号从下方去掉，而最古老的义项是给人定名的人。

intro.en: Denominator is a Latin agent noun on a verb of naming; its root, prefix and suffix all build English words.
intro.cn: denominator 是建立在「命名」动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根、前缀与后缀都构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen gives nominal, nomination, misnomer and denomination; the prefix de- and the agent ending -tor complete the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nomen 衍生 nominal、nomination、misnomer 与 denomination；前缀 de- 与施动词尾 -tor 补全了这个词。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供命名的动作。

items.example: The verb turns the name into an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把名字变成动作。

items.example: The prefix makes the naming specific.

items.meaning: one who names; the naming number
items.example: The denominator names the part size.
The unit was denominated in grams.

items.meaning: a name; a religious body; a money value
items.example: The notes come in several denominations.
The nominal fee was one coin.
items.exampleCN: 名义费用只是一枚硬币。

items.example: It also forms numerator and operator.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 numerator 与 operator。

命名；给……定名（同出拉丁 denominare）
名称；教派；面额（同出拉丁 denominare）
名义上的；标称的（同出拉丁 nomen）
用词不当；错误名称（同出拉丁 nomen）

definition_zh: 各种各样的；多种多样的（强调种类彼此不同）
definition_en: several different kinds of one broad thing, differing from one another in form or character
core_image: 同一片果园里，早熟与晚熟的苹果挂在不同枝头，果皮一红一黄
scene: 果园主人把早熟与晚熟的苹果分栽在两侧，果皮一个偏红一个偏黄，装箱时分开贴标签。 The orchard grows a variety of apples, some ripening early and some late.
sceneCN: 这里指同一类水果的不同品种（第 2 个义项：同一事物的不同变体）；句意为这座果园种植多个品种的苹果，有的早熟有的晚熟。图中可辨识物件：分栽两侧的果树、红黄不同的果皮、分开的标签。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）各种各样的；多种多样的

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「多样性、品种」
由同一拉丁词根加形容词尾构成，义为「各种各样的」
由同一词根加动词尾构成，义为「变化、使不同」
由词根加形容词尾构成，义为「可变的；变量」
由词根加名词尾构成，义为「变体」

senses.title: Kinds on offer
senses.definition: to include many kinds of goods or things
senses.definitionCN: 指包含许多种货物或事物
senses.example: The stall sells a variety of cheeses, each with a different age.
senses.exampleCN: 这个摊位出售各种各样的奶酪，每一种的成熟期都不同。
senses.why: Var- carries the idea of difference, so the phrase counts kinds rather than measuring a span.
senses.whyCN: var- 带着「差异」的意思，所以这个短语数的是种类，而不是量跨度。

senses.title: Forms of one thing
senses.definition: to exist in several forms of a single type
senses.definitionCN: 指同一类型以好几种形式存在
senses.example: The same story appears in a variety of versions across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 同一个故事在这个地区以多种版本出现。
senses.why: Difference inside one family is the heart of the word, and this sense keeps the family name.
senses.whyCN: 同一族内部的差异是这个词的核心，这个义项保留着族名。

senses.title: Many uses
senses.definition: to serve several different purposes
senses.definitionCN: 指可以承担好几种不同用途
senses.example: Oil serves a variety of purposes, from cooking to machine lubrication.
senses.exampleCN: 油有许多种用途，从烹饪到机器润滑。
senses.why: Uses differ in kind, so the phrase fits better than a word about length.
senses.whyCN: 用途的差别在种类上，所以这个短语比讲长度的词更合适。

senses.title: Many opinions
senses.definition: to include several differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指包含好几种不同的看法
senses.example: A variety of opinions was recorded before the committee voted.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表决之前，记录下了多种意见。
senses.why: Opinion is where variety becomes social, and the phrase treats views as so many kinds.
senses.whyCN: 意见是多样性变成社会性的地方，这个短语把看法当作一个个种类。

senses.title: Many breeds or species
senses.definition: to include several cultivated varieties or natural species
senses.definitionCN: 指包含好几种栽培品种或自然物种
senses.example: Farmers here keep a variety of old wheat strains that resist dry weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民保留着多种耐旱的老麦种。
senses.why: Agriculture uses the word for cultivated kinds, which is the most literal sense of variety.
senses.whyCN: 农业用它指栽培品种，这是 variety 最本色的义项。

senses.title: Language variants
senses.definition: to appear in several regional or social forms
senses.definitionCN: 指以好几种地域或社会形式出现
senses.example: The language is spoken in a variety of forms along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海地区这门语言以多种形式被使用。
senses.why: A language splits into kinds without splitting into different languages, and the word holds both.
senses.whyCN: 一门语言会分成许多种类，却仍是一门语言，这个词把两者都握住。

senses.title: Many methods
senses.definition: to offer several different ways of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 指提供好几种不同的做法
senses.example: A variety of methods was tried before the simplest one worked.
senses.exampleCN: 在最简单的办法奏效之前，试过多种方法。
senses.why: Methods are tools of different makes, and the phrase sorts them by make.
senses.whyCN: 方法是不同做法的工具，这个短语按「做法」来分类。

senses.title: Varied experience
senses.definition: to include many different experiences within one life or account
senses.definitionCN: 指在一个人生或叙述里包含许多不同的经历
senses.example: Her account of the voyage records a variety of encounters, from storms to kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 她对航行的记述记录了多种遭遇，从风暴到善意。
senses.why: The word can count events as kinds, which is how it moves from goods to a life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能把事件当作种类来数，于是从货物走到了人生。

intro.en: Variety came from Latin varietas, diversity, from varius, varied or spotted. The deeper origin of varius is uncertain; one older suggestion links it to varix, a swollen vein, but no single account is accepted. English borrowed the word through French in the fifteenth century, and the collocation a variety of is modern.
intro.cn: variety 出自拉丁语 varietas「多样性」，而后者来自 varius「杂色的、多变的」。varius 的更早来源不确定，一种较早的说法把它与 varix「静脉曲张」联系起来，但没有哪一家得到公认。英语十五世纪经法语借入这个词，而「a variety of」是近代搭配。

items.en: Varius meant varied, spotted or changeable, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: varius 意为多变的、杂色的，它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: One older proposal connects varius with varix, a swollen vein, but the link is not established and the question stays open.
items.cn: 一种较早的说法把 varius 与 varix「静脉曲张」联系起来，但这一联系并未确立，问题仍悬着。

items.en: Varietas named diversity itself, the quality of being of several kinds.
items.cn: varietas 命名的是多样性本身，即「属于好几种」的性质。

items.en: French passed the word to English in the fifteenth century, still meaning diversity.
items.cn: 法语在十五世纪把这个词传给英语，仍表示多样性。

items.en: A variety of became a standard quantity phrase in the nineteenth century, used of goods, opinions and methods.
items.cn: 「a variety of」在十九世纪成为标准量词短语，用于货物、意见与方法。

note.en: The first group shares the varied root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of plurality and breadth.
note.cn: 第一组共享「多变」词根；第二组是与「多样、广度」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Diversity, or a particular kind within a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指多样性，或群体中的某一品种。

entries.definition: Several different, used directly before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指好几个不同的，直接放在名词前。

entries.definition: To change or make different.
entries.definitionCN: 指变化或使不同。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a quantity that can change.
entries.definitionCN: 指可变的，或可变的量。

entries.definition: A different form of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一事物的不同形式。

entries.definition: Breadth from one end to the other, stressing span rather than difference.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一端到另一端的广度，强调跨度而非差异。

entries.definition: A mixed selection put together, often of small items.
entries.definitionCN: 指搭配起来的一批混合选择，多用于小物件。

entries.definition: A chosen set from a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指从更大整体中挑出的一组。

entries.definition: Different elements combined in one mass.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同成分混在一起。

entries.definition: Clearly different from one another.
entries.definitionCN: 指彼此明显不同。

entries.definition: A full spread between opposite ends.
entries.definitionCN: 指对立两端之间的完整分布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the spotted-cloth picture behind varius, the family-of-kinds idea, and the contrast with range.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用拉丁词根「斑驳的布」这一画面、「同族不同种」的想法，以及和「范围」一词的对照来记。

normal.en: Varius means spotted or changeable, like cloth dyed unevenly, so variety is many shades in one cloth.
normal.cn: varius 意为斑驳的、多变的，像染得不匀的布，所以 variety 就是一块布上有许多深浅。

normal.en: Variety counts kinds; range measures span; a shop can have both.
normal.cn: variety 数种类，range 量跨度，一家店可以两样都有。

normal.en: Various goes straight before a noun, while a variety of is a noun phrase that takes of.
normal.cn: various 直接放在名词前，a variety of 是带 of 的名词短语。

normal.en: Apples are the best picture: one fruit, many named kinds.
normal.cn: 苹果是最好的画面：一种水果，许多有名字的品种。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variety the noun, various the adjective, and they all point to difference.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variety 是名词，various 是形容词，都指向差异。

abstract.en: Variety is difference that can still be counted as one family.
abstract.cn: 多样性是仍能被算作一个家族的差异。

abstract.en: A market with many kinds is richer than a market with many of one kind.
abstract.cn: 许多种类的集市，比同一种类摆得很多的集市更丰富。

abstract.en: To record a variety of encounters is to admit that no single meeting explains the voyage.
abstract.cn: 记下多种遭遇，就是承认没有哪一次相遇能解释整趟航行。

examples.en: The course attracts students from a variety of backgrounds.
examples.cn: 这门课吸引来自各种背景的学生。

examples.en: A variety of methods can be used to measure the same quantity.
examples.cn: 可以用多种方法测量同一个量。

examples.en: The garden contains a variety of herbs, each with its own scent.
examples.cn: 这座园子里有各种各样的香草，每一种都有自己的气味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 瓦莱厄提 奥夫」——一块布上深浅不一：各种各样的

root: 拉丁语 varius「杂色的、多变的」（更早来源不确定，一说与 varix「静脉曲张」有关）→ varietas「多样性」，经法语进入英语；同族 vary、various、variable、variant。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all count differing kinds: goods, forms of one thing, uses, opinions, breeds, language variants, methods and varied experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在数不同的种类：商品、同一事物的形式、用途、意见、品种、语言变体、方法与多样的经历。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one orchard, many apple kinds, red and yellow on different branches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座果园，许多苹果品种，红与黄挂在不同枝头。

branches.en: THE STALL: many kinds of one good are offered side by side.
branches.cn: 摊位：同一种货品摆出许多种类。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: one story has many versions under one name.
branches.cn: 家族：同一个故事在一个名字下有好几个版本。

branches.en: THE USE AND THE VIEW: oil serves many purposes, and a committee records many opinions.
branches.cn: 用途与看法：油有许多用途，委员会记下许多意见。

branches.en: THE BREED AND THE TONGUE: old wheat strains differ, and one language takes several forms.
branches.cn: 品种与语言：老麦种彼此不同，一门语言有几种形式。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND THE LIFE: many ways are tried, and one voyage holds many encounters.
branches.cn: 方法与人生：试过许多办法，一趟航行容纳许多遭遇。

intro.en: The family grows from one Latin adjective of difference, with endings marking noun, adjective and verb.
intro.cn: 这个词族从一个表示差异的拉丁形容词长出来，词尾标出名词、形容词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and varietas supply the core; -ety, -ous, -able and -ant build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 varius 与 varietas 提供核心，-ety、-ous、-able 与 -ant 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的根，更早来源不确定。

items.example: It is the direct source of variety.
items.exampleCN: 它是 variety 的直接来源。

items.example: It stands behind the English verb vary.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词 vary 背后的词。

items.example: It forms variety from the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁名词构成 variety。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「多样性、品种」
由同一词根加形容词尾构成，义为「各种各样的」
由同一词根加动词尾构成，义为「变化」
由词根加形容词尾构成，义为「可变的；变量」
由词根加名词尾构成，义为「变体」

definition_zh: 放大（声音、信号）；增强；详述；扩充；夸大
definition_en: to make larger, stronger or louder; to expand in detail
core_image: 一只小喇叭把耳语推成一屋子都听得见的声音
scene: 礼堂后排听不清，工作人员把台上的小盒子调高了一档。 A small box on the desk can amplify the speaker's voice for the back rows.
sceneCN: 这里指把声音放大（第 1 个义项：使声音变响）；句意为桌上的小盒子把讲者的声音放大，供后排听清。

pos.zh: 放大；增强；详述；扩充；夸大

senses.title: To make sound louder
senses.definition: to increase the volume of sound
senses.definitionCN: 提高声音的音量
senses.example: The hall amplifies every whisper.
senses.exampleCN: 这间大厅会把每一声耳语放大。
senses.why: Amplificare joined amplus, large, with facere, to make, so the word first meant to make something large.
senses.whyCN: amplificare 把 amplus「大的」与 facere「做」结合，因此这个词最早意为「使变大」。

senses.title: To strengthen a signal
senses.definition: to raise the strength of an electrical or radio signal
senses.definitionCN: 提高电信号或无线电信号的强度
senses.example: The repeater amplifies the weak signal.
senses.exampleCN: 中继器把微弱信号增强。
senses.why: Electronics gave the old word a measurable quantity to enlarge.
senses.whyCN: 电子学给了这个旧词一个可测量的「量」去放大。

senses.title: To intensify an effect
senses.definition: to make an effect stronger or more vivid
senses.definitionCN: 使效果更强、更鲜明
senses.example: Cold air amplifies the smell of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 冷空气让海的味道更浓。
senses.why: Once size becomes strength, anything with intensity can be amplified.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「大」变成「强」，任何有强度的事物都能被放大。

senses.title: To expand in detail
senses.definition: to add detail to a statement or theme
senses.definitionCN: 给陈述或主题补充细节
senses.example: The speaker amplified her point with two examples.
senses.exampleCN: 讲者用两个例子详述了她的观点。
senses.why: Rhetoric used the word for filling out a theme, making it large in words.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学用这个词表示把主题铺开，使其在言辞上变大。

senses.title: To exaggerate
senses.definition: to make something seem larger or worse than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物显得比实际更大或更糟
senses.example: The report amplifies the danger beyond the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把危险夸大到证据之外。
senses.why: The same enlarging act becomes a fault when it outruns the facts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「放大」动作一旦超出事实，就成了过失。

senses.title: To multiply DNA
senses.definition: to make many copies of a DNA sequence
senses.definitionCN: 把一段脱氧核糖核酸序列复制成许多份
senses.example: The lab amplifies a short fragment of the gene.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室扩增了该基因的一小段。
senses.why: Molecular biology uses amplification for copying, an exact technical enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 分子生物学用「扩增」表示复制，是一种精确的技术性放大。

senses.title: To raise current or voltage
senses.definition: to increase the amplitude of an electrical wave
senses.definitionCN: 增大电波的振幅
senses.example: The circuit amplifies the current before it reaches the coil.
senses.exampleCN: 电路在电流到达线圈之前将其放大。
senses.why: The word amplitude itself comes from the same large-stem.
senses.whyCN: amplitude 一词本身也出自同一个表示「大」的词干。

senses.title: To fill out a rhetorical theme
senses.definition: to develop a theme at length for effect
senses.definitionCN: 为效果而把一个主题长时间展开
senses.example: The old manuals teach students to amplify a proverb.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时手册教学生把一句谚语铺陈成文。
senses.why: Ancient rhetoric named this exercise amplification, and English kept the verb.
senses.whyCN: 古代修辞学把这套练习称为铺陈，英语保留了动词。

intro.en: Amplify comes from Latin amplificare, to enlarge, from amplus, large, plus facere, to make. The direct source is clear; the origin of amplus itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: amplify 来自拉丁 amplificare「使变大」，由 amplus「大的」与 facere「做」构成。直接来源清楚；amplus 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Amplus meant large, spacious or ample; its deeper origin is a reconstruction and is source uncertain.
items.cn: amplus 意为大的、宽敞的、充足的；其更深来源属重构，来源不确定。

items.en: The combining form -ficare comes from facere, to make, so amplificare is to make large.
items.cn: 组合形式 -ficare 来自 facere「做」，因此 amplificare 就是「使变大」。

items.en: The verb meant to enlarge, increase or widen, and rhetoric used it for expanding a theme.
items.cn: 这个动词意为扩大、增加、拓宽，修辞学用它表示展开主题。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun amplifier was coined for devices that raise signal strength in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 名词 amplifier 在二十世纪被造出，指提高信号强度的装置。

items.en: The same verb now names the copying of DNA, where enlargement is exact multiplication.
items.cn: 同一个动词如今命名 DNA 的复制，那里的「放大」是精确的倍增。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin large-making stem; the second group names ways of adding size, strength or detail.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「使变大」的词干；第二组是增加规模、强度或细节的近义说法。

entries.definition: The act of enlarging sound, signal or detail.
entries.definitionCN: 放大声音、信号或细节的行为。

entries.definition: A device that raises the strength of a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 提高信号强度的装置。

entries.definition: The size of a wave's swing, from the same large-stem.
entries.definitionCN: 波摆动的幅度，出自同一「大」词干。

entries.definition: More than enough in size or supply.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或供给上绰绰有余。

entries.definition: To make something look bigger, especially through a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物看起来更大，尤指通过透镜。

entries.definition: To make stronger in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 使程度更强。

entries.definition: To grow larger in size or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或范围上变大。

entries.definition: To raise or push up, often a signal or level.
entries.definitionCN: 提高、推高，常指信号或水平。

entries.definition: To describe something as larger than it is.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物说得比实际更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Amplificare is amplus plus facere: to make large.
normal.cn: amplificare 是 amplus 加 facere：使变大。

normal.en: The amplifier is the device, and amplification is the act.
normal.cn: amplifier 是装置，amplification 是行为。

normal.en: The word runs from sound to signal to feeling to detail to genetic copying.
normal.cn: 这个词从声音走到信号、感受、细节，再到基因复制。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: amplify the sound, amplify a signal, amplify a point.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：放大声音、增强信号、详述要点。

normal.en: Amplify is not augment: one magnifies what is there, the other adds more to it.
normal.cn: amplify 不是 augment：前者放大已有之物，后者往里添更多。

abstract.en: Amplify is a bell that turns a small tap into a sound across the valley.
abstract.cn: 放大是一口钟，把轻轻一碰变成满谷的声音。

abstract.en: The same act can serve truth or falsehood, depending on what is fed in.
abstract.cn: 同一个放大动作既能服务真相，也能服务谎言，取决于输入什么。

abstract.en: To amplify is to make a thing more itself, not to make it another thing.
abstract.cn: 放大是让事物更像它自己，而不是变成别的东西。

examples.en: The microphone can amplify a voice without changing its tone.
examples.cn: 麦克风能把声音放大，却不改变音色。

examples.en: The lost keys seemed to amplify the worry of the whole family.
examples.cn: 钥匙丢了，全家的担忧仿佛被放大了。

examples.en: The essay uses three pages to amplify one short proverb.
examples.cn: 这篇文章用三页篇幅铺陈一句短谚语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安普利法艾」——安个小喇叭，声音放到最大：放大

root: 拉丁 amplificare「使变大」← amplus「大的、宽敞的」+ -ficare（来自 facere「做」）。amplus 更深来源属重构，来源不确定；英语十五世纪借入，确切首见年代不确定。同族 amplitude、ample 与 amplifier 共用「大」的词干；现代又用于电子信号与 DNA 扩增。与 augment 不同：amplify 放大已有之物，augment 另行添加。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses enlarge sound, signal, effect, detail, a claim, DNA, current and a rhetorical theme.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分别放大声音、信号、效果、细节、说法、脱氧核糖核酸、电流与修辞主题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small horn that turns a whisper into a room-filling sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小喇叭把耳语变成满屋都听得见的声音。

branches.en: THE SOUND AND THE CURRENT: louder volume and a larger electrical swing.
branches.cn: 声音与电流：更大的音量与更大的电波振幅。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: a weak carrier made strong enough to travel.
branches.cn: 信号：把微弱载波增强到能传远。

branches.en: THE STRONGER EFFECT: intensity raised, and a claim pushed past the facts.
branches.cn: 更强的效果：强度被提高，说法被推到事实之外。

branches.en: THE FULLER THEME: a point filled out and an old rhetorical exercise.
branches.cn: 更饱满的主题：被补充细节的要点与古老的修辞练习。

branches.en: THE COPIED GENE: exact multiplication in the laboratory.
branches.cn: 被复制的基因：实验室里的精确倍增。

intro.en: Amplify is Latin amplificare, with amplus and facere both visible inside the verb.
intro.cn: amplify 是拉丁 amplificare，动词内部两个构件 amplus 与 facere 都看得见。

latinIntro.en: Amplus supplies the size, -ficare supplies the making, and the noun amplification keeps the act.
latinIntro.cn: amplus 提供「大」，-ficare 提供「做」，名词 amplification 保留这一行为。

items.example: The adjective supplies the size that is to be increased.
items.exampleCN: 形容词提供待增大的规模。

items.example: The verb supplies the making in -ficare.
items.exampleCN: 动词在 -ficare 中提供「制造」。

items.example: The form turns an adjective into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式把形容词变成「使…」的动词。

items.example: Latin already used it for widening and for rhetoric.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语已用它表示拓宽与修辞铺陈。

items.example: The noun names the act rather than the device.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名行为，而非装置。

items.meaning: a device that raises a signal
items.example: The agent suffix names the thing that does the work.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀命名干这件事的物件。

items.example: The noun measures how far a wave moves.
The adjective keeps the plain sense of size.
items.exampleCN: 形容词保留「大」的平实义。

items.example: It also builds simplify, clarify and verify.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 simplify、clarify 与 verify。

definition_zh: n. 名人，名流；名声，名气
definition_en: a famous person; the state of being famous
core_image: 闪光灯围住一张熟悉的脸
scene: 闪光灯一亮，这位名人在红毯上停下脚步。 The celebrity paused on the red carpet as the cameras flashed.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：celebrity 指名人；句意是名人在红毯上被闪光灯围住。

pos.zh: 名人；名声

senses.title: A famous person
senses.definition: a person who is well known to the public
senses.definitionCN: 为公众熟知的人
senses.example: The restaurant is popular with celebrities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅很受名人欢迎。
senses.why: The word came from Latin celeber, crowded or famous.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 celeber（热闹的、著名的）。

senses.title: The state of being famous
senses.definition: the condition of being widely known
senses.definitionCN: 被广泛知晓的状态
senses.example: The film brought her sudden celebrity.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影让她一夜成名。
senses.why: The abstract sense came before the person sense.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义先于名人义出现。

intro.en: Celebrity comes from Latin celebritas, fame, from celeber, crowded or well known.
intro.cn: celebrity 源自拉丁语 celebritas（名声），来自 celeber（热闹的、著名的）。

items.en: Latin celeber means crowded or famous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celeber 意为热闹的或著名的。

items.en: Celebritas names fame.
items.cn: celebritas 指名声。

items.en: English celebrity first means a solemn rite.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语最初指庄严仪式。

items.en: The word settles into the sense of fame.
items.cn: 十七世纪固定为名声义。

items.en: Film and television create modern celebrities.
items.cn: 二十世纪影视造就现代名人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the celebr- stem; the near-meaning group separates fame from the famous person.
note.cn: 形近组共享 celebr- 词干；近义组区分名声与名人。

entries.definition: To mark a happy event.
entries.definitionCN: 庆祝。

entries.definition: A joyful public event.
entries.definitionCN: 庆祝活动。

entries.definition: Swiftness of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速。

entries.definition: The state of being known.
entries.definitionCN: 名声。

entries.definition: A very famous performer.
entries.definitionCN: 明星。

entries.definition: Someone known to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 公众人物。

normalIntro.en: A celebrity is a face the crowd already knows.
normalIntro.cn: celebrity 是人群早已认得的一张脸。

normal.en: Celeber meant crowded or famous.
normal.cn: celeber 意为热闹的或著名的。

normal.en: Celebritas meant fame.
normal.cn: celebritas 意为名声。

normal.en: A celebrity is a famous person.
normal.cn: celebrity 是名人。

normal.en: Cameras follow the face everywhere.
normal.cn: 相机到处跟着这张脸。

normal.en: The word also means the fame itself.
normal.cn: 这个词也指名声本身。

abstract.en: A name larger than its owner.
abstract.cn: 比本人更大的一个名字。

abstract.en: Privacy traded for light.
abstract.cn: 用隐私换来的光。

abstract.en: Being known by strangers.
abstract.cn: 被陌生人认识。

examples.en: The charity dinner attracted several celebrities.
examples.cn: 这场慈善晚宴吸引了几位名人。

examples.en: Celebrity brought her money but little peace.
examples.cn: 名声给她带来金钱，却少有安宁。

examples.en: He never enjoyed his sudden celebrity.
examples.cn: 他从不享受突如其来的名声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞了布里提」——人群塞满布里，只为看一个名人。

root: 拉丁语 celeber（著名的）→ celebritas（名声）→ 英语 celebrity

sensesIntro.en: Fame came first as a word, and then it named the people who carry it.
sensesIntro.cn: 名声先有词，后来才用来称承载名声的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar face inside a ring of flashes
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈闪光灯中的一张熟脸

branches.en: A red carpet lined with cameras.
branches.cn: 排满相机的红毯。

branches.en: A chef whose name sells books.
branches.cn: 名字能卖书的主厨。

branches.en: A sudden fame after one film.
branches.cn: 一部电影后的骤然成名。

branches.en: A quiet life lost to fame.
branches.cn: 被名声夺走的安静生活。

branches.en: Fame walking around on two legs.
branches.cn: 长了腿到处走的名声。

fama 产生 fame 与 famous。
